result: This archive has now found the tree six years out on two Mazza births and eleven years out on Giovanni Arena. A wrong year is the likelier explanation than a wrong town.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1866–1913
scope: FORTY-EIGHT volumes, not eight. This archive had recorded the series as starting in 1905; it starts in 1866. 1885, 1886, 1887, 1889, 1890, 1891, 1892, 1893 and 1894 have been read; 1888 is water-damaged across the A entries and cannot be.
result: Two Arena weddings found in 1885. Rocco Arena × Generosa Costa still missing; Giovanni Polistena × Nunziata Donato and Michele Donato's marriage are now both inside the window and unsearched.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1866–1943
scope: EIGHTY-ONE volumes, and this archive did not know they existed. The annual index gives a patronymic — «di X» where the father lives, «fu X» where he does not — as well as the act number. The A block has been read for 1889–1896 and for 1897–1908.
result: BOTH OF THEM FOUND AND THE ROW CLOSES. FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA, Morti 1901 atto 96, dead 29 August 1901; SERAFINA ARLOTTA, Morti 1908 atto 55, dead 24 April 1908 — both at VIA GROTTE NUMBER TWO. Twenty years of index reading, and the two acts are in the same house. Six unread Arena leads came out of the sweep and are listed on the sweep's own row.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni pubblicazioni 1866–1913
scope: FORTY-SIX volumes of banns, each with its own annual index — which is how the 1888 marriage was found when the marriage index itself was destroyed by water across exactly the A entries.
result: Arena Rocco / Costa Generosa, under A in the 1888 banns index. Everything else in the series is unread.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1874–1878
scope: The first search the corrected coverage note made possible: Michele Donato's marriage, about 1875–77. Indexes read for 1874, 1876, 1877 and 1878; 1875 has no index at all and its acts 3–26 were scanned by the margin boxes.
result: NEGATIVE. No Donato Michele among the grooms. But Donato Candeloro marries in 1874 and again in 1877, Donato Bruno in 1878 and a Donato Carmela in 1875 — so the Donato were a Scilla family all along, and the idea that the surname arrived late is dead.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1871 and Nati 1845
scope: The marriage of Rosario Mazza and Leonarda Bonanno, and Rosario's own birth. Found by abandoning the parish film: civil registration began in the south in 1866, so a marriage of about 1870 is a CIVIL act.

Nati 1845 atto 64 — born 2 June 1845, father Mariano, 36, bracciale, mother Maria Catalano, 36. The tree's 1850 is five years out.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Matrimoni 1820–1845
scope: Twenty-six consecutive years, the whole civil series from its first volume, read for a Mazza groom.
result: EXACTLY ONE in twenty-six years: Mariano Mazza, act 17 of 1836, to Agata Catalano of Macchia, «figlio di IGNAZIO e di GIUSEPPA PULVIRENTI». Recorded as a LEAD, not a fact — the bride is Agata where Rosario's acts say Maria, and the groom's age is three years out. Innocenzio Mazza did not marry there either.

source: Antenati — Piedimonte Etneo, Nati 1844, 1845, 1846, 1847
scope: Four years read ENTIRE — over five hundred births — for brothers and sisters of Rosario Mazza.
result: HE HAS NONE THERE. Mariano Mazza and Maria Catalano appear once, at act 64 of 1845. The only other Mazza births belong to Innocenzio Mazza and Domenica Cavallaro — the couple the archive's OTHER Piedimonte Mazza line descends from, which raises the question whether Ignazio's sons were Mariano and Innocenzio.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1854, act located by arithmetic
scope: The 1854 Tavola carries no act numbers. Two acts to an opening, act = 66 + 2×(image−36), which puts late April at images 39–41.
result: ACT 76. Giovanni Arena born 30 April 1854, declared by his grandfather GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, 75, marinaro, «figlio del fu DOMENICO». The Tavola said «Rosa Arlotta» and 20 April and was wrong twice. Giovanni Arena is Rocco's FULL BROTHER, and DOMENICO ARLOTTA is the deepest name on the Calabrian side.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1885 and 1888
scope: The corrected coverage note opened forty-eight volumes. 1885 for the Arena weddings; 1888 for Rocco Arena's own.
result: THREE ACTS. 1885 atto 73 and atto 86: two of Rocco's brothers married seven weeks apart. 1888 atto 63: ROCCO ARENA'S OWN MARRIAGE ACT names his parents outright — Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta — and gives Generosa Costa's parents for the first time, Antonio Costa and ANNA ARLOTTA.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni pubblicazioni 1888
scope: The 1888 marriage index is destroyed by water across exactly the A entries. The BANNS are a separate series of 46 volumes with their own annual index.
result: THE WAY ROUND A DESTROYED INDEX. Publication 63, 18 November 1888: Francesco Antonio Arena appears IN PERSON, alive, sixty-eight, a pescatore, a week short of sixty-nine. And the couple swore there was no impediment of kinship — so Rocco and Generosa were NOT first cousins.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Nati 1855
scope: The year nobody had read. The archive had read 1851 (the tree's date), 1856 and 1859 (a declared age) and closed the search.
result: MICHELE DONATO, BORN 3 OCTOBER 1855, act 163 — «DOMENICO DONATO, figlio di CANDELORO, trentotto, marinaro» and «NUNZIATA SOFI, trentasette». Three generations in one act, the ages exact at both ends, and the longest open question in the archive answered.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1889–1896 (recorded at the time as 1889–1902)
scope: Eighty-one volumes of deaths, 1866–1943, that this archive did not know existed. The annual index carries a PATRONYMIC as well as a name.
result: CORRECTED 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. This row was written as «neither Francesco Antonio Arena nor Serafina Arlotta in thirteen years». FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA DIED IN 1901, act 96, inside the span this row claimed to have cleared. Either those later indexes were read and he was missed, or — far more likely, since the containers for 1897–1908 were still being bought three days later — the row counted years it had not opened. It does not matter which: A NEGATIVE IS ONLY WORTH THE PAGES ACTUALLY TURNED, and this one was written wider than its evidence. The years this archive can stand behind are 1889–1896. What the row did genuinely find stands: Fortunato Arena (ten days old, Via Grotte 70), Maria Donato (twenty-eight months, Via Grotte 21) and Orazio Arena — who turns out NOT to be the tree's Orazio.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1874–1885 and 1838–1847
scope: Michele Donato's own marriage, eleven years; and his parents' marriage, six years.
result: BOTH NEGATIVE, and both informative. Michele is neither born nor married at Scilla in the window — he came from elsewhere already married. And 1843 act 11 shows a DONATO ANTONIO «figlio di BRUNO»: there are at least TWO Donato lines in the town, which is why the Donato marriages of the 1870s are numerous and none is his.

source: FamilySearch — the New Orleans manifest of the Liguria, 1908, BOTH PAGES
scope: American manifests from 1907 are two-page forms. This archive had only ever read page one.
result: THE VERSO CARRIES COLUMN 29, PLACE OF BIRTH. Against line 15, Michele Donato: «R. Calabria / Scilla». Lines 9–11 of the same sheet say Tresilico, so the clerk was distinguishing. That sent the search back to the Scilla registers, where it belonged.

source: FindMyPast — passenger lists, marriages, censuses, parish index
scope: A one-week trial. Twenty-six outcomes recorded.
result: Rocco Arena's four crossings named and shipped (Elysia 1892, Suevia 1894, Trave 1900, San Guglielmo 1913) and the 1894 no longer «probable». The 1913 manifest's RELATION columns name his wife and a nephew. Rocco Arlotta, the 1900 lodger, identified by his marriage and confirmed by his children's names. AND ONE RETRACTION: the Clementina Arena crossing this archive had held for months belongs to another family.

source: The archive's own negatives, audited
scope: Nine negatives re-read — not repeated, but examined for what set each window.
result: FIVE HAD ALREADY FAILED. Every failed window came from a declared age or an assumed eldest child. The rule: widen such a window by at least five years in both directions before a negative inside it means anything. Published at /audit.

source: Antenati — Vibo Valentia, Briatico and Soriano Calabro

result: Would convert eight asserted generations into documented ones. The largest single gap in this archive.

result: 1874 CANNOT BE READ — the volume carries «pag. ondulate, pag. macchiata, tutto il volume, impossibile fare di meglio» and the index is a black wash. He died in 1874 or after 1877.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1848–1854

source: Trove — the Brisbane Italian community
scope: Arrivals, naturalisations, the 1942 internments, and the Queensland Italian press.
result: One mention in this archive. The Australian end of all four quarters is almost unsourced.

source: Queensland BDM — beyond the six registrations
scope: The Nudgee end of every one of the four quarters, searched on parents' names rather than the person's.
result: Three mentions. The index is free and the technique that produced six registrations has not been run out. DONE 15 SEPTEMBER. All ten surnames swept by exact surname across births, marriages and deaths. The find was the CRUPI -- three brothers of Angela nobody here knew about. The rest is the shape of the index rather than of the family: POLISTENA and ANILE return NOTHING AT ALL and PROSTAMO returns ONE record, because births stop in 1926, marriages in 1951 and deaths in 1996 and these people arrived in 1949. ARENA returns seventy-five and not one is ours -- an Irish-Australian family entirely unconnected to Scilla.

source: Find a Grave — Nudgee Catholic cemetery
scope: Photographs and inscriptions against the nineteen burials the Archdiocese register gave.
result: Two mentions. An inscription often carries a birth date the register does not.

source: NARA New York — Rocco Arena's naturalisation

result: FindMyPast's petition set begins too late for him. This is a National Archives job, not a subscription one.

source: The Catholic Heritage Archive — Our Lady of Loretto transcripts
scope: Eighty-four Arena baptisms are indexed and readable; the transcripts, which carry the MOTHER'S NAME and the GODPARENTS, are a higher subscription tier.
result: Godparents in an emigrant parish are almost always kin. They would settle at a stroke whether the Giovanni Arena baptising a child in 1900 is Rocco's brother.

source: Geneanet — surname sweep
scope: PROSTAMO, MELLUSO, ANILE, VENTRICE, ARLOTTA searched across all Geneanet record sets (trees, archives, transcriptions).
result: No holding touches this family. PROSTAMO returns eight entries, every one a New Haven or Hamden, Connecticut vital record 1914-1955 — an American cluster of the surname, untested against Briatico and claimed as nothing. MELLUSO (506) is an Agrigento family. VENTRICE (730) is Ustica and French Algeria. ARLOTTA (881) is Buffalo, New York. ANILE (476) clusters at Pizzo, eleven km from Briatico, but no entry reaches our people.

result: Piedimonte Etneo holds 1,703 individuals, Briatico 132. Both are user-submitted trees, heavily from single uploaders (pigellino74, rcparedes). Not sources; leads at best.

source: Antenati — Briatico, Nati 1818

result: NEGATIVE, and complete. No child of any given name carries the surname Prostamo. The index is alphabetised by the child's GIVEN name, so the absence is of the surname from the year entirely, not of one Domenico.

source: Antenati — Briatico, Nati 1819
scope: The whole year read: 34 births, all three Tavola pages.
result: NEGATIVE, and complete. No Prostamo among the 34. Two Anile households appear (Giuseppe Anile and Annunziata Polito; Vincenzo Anile and Rosaria Francica) — the surname is documented in Briatico, which it had not been before.

source: Antenati — the Potenzoni discovery
scope: Searched the register index on localita=Potenzoni after three straight years of Briatico births turned up no Prostamo at all.
result: POTENZONI IS ITS OWN COMUNE ON ANTENATI, WITH 57 REGISTERS. It is a frazione of Briatico and it kept its own civil register from 1806. Everything read at Briatico so far has been the wrong parish if the family lived there. Births 1812-1837 are a single 364-image volume; marriages 1812-1858 a single 293-image volume; and the marriage allegati 1812-1850 hold the spouses' own birth certificates. This is the largest unopened door in the Calabrian half of the archive.

source: Antenati — Potenzoni, Nati 1812-1837
scope: 364 images, an_ua37927182 / container 0AQJBAW. Domenico Prostamo, born about 1820, would fall in it.
result: SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY. This was opened on the reasoning that Domenico Prostamo, born about 1820, must be in the frazione if he was not in Briatico. His marriage act of 1849 then said he was NATO IN PIZZO and born in 1814. The volume is mapped and the mapping is kept, but this family is not in it.

source: Antenati — Potenzoni, Matrimoni 1812-1858
scope: 293 images, an_ua37923835 / container 5K1ln7r. Domenico Prostamo married Giovanna Ventrice somewhere in this span.
result: SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY. Domenico Prostamo married Giovanna Ventrice at BRIATICO on 14 June 1849, act 1 — found in the Briatico register, not this one. The Potenzoni mapping is kept for whoever needs that comune.

source: Antenati — Potenzoni, Nati: the volume opened and mapped
scope: an_ua37927182 / container 0AQJBAW, 364 images. Located the annual blocks: fourteen images to a year, two acts to an opening, each year closed by a Rubrica listing every birth in date order. 1818 index at image 66, 1819 at 80, 1820 at 104-106.
result: PARTIAL. Potenzoni 1818 read in full (entries 12-21) and 1820 read in part (entries 7-16 of 23). No Prostamo in either. Two cautions recorded for whoever continues: the photographer left the 1819 Tavola and a title sheet lying on top of EVERY frame in this run, so the printed year visible at the head of an image is not the year of the page beneath it; and the volume is not purely Potenzoni — the register bound in at image 106 is headed «Comune di Briatico», for 1822, which suggests these are the second originals deposited with the tribunal and that Briatico years sit inside the Potenzoni unit.

source: Antenati — Briatico, Matrimoni 1840, 1841, 1842
scope: Read by cropping the parroco's right-hand certificate box, which names both spouses, from every page and montaging them.
result: NEGATIVE for Prostamo. 1840 has three marriages, 1841 about five, 1842 thirteen. Act 8 of 1842 was opened in full to test a suspected Prostamo in the margin: it is Giuseppe Artesi, 19, son of the late Nicola Artesi and Nicolina Corassi, marrying Alfonsina Petrarca, 15, born at Pizzinni, daughter of the late Francesco Antonio Petrarca and the late Rosa Arena. Not ours. The suspected name was a misreading of a 240-pixel thumbnail and was never claimed.

source: Trove — Prostamo, all collections
scope: Keyword PROSTAMO across newspapers, gazettes, books, archives and people.
result: ELEVEN newspaper and gazette results, and the useful ones are all Commonwealth Gazette naturalisations at Brisbane: ASSUNTA MARIA PROSTAMO of 3 Frank Street, Graceville, naturalised 4 July 1966; DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO of 38 Park Terrace, Sherwood, naturalised 1 October 1962; and ANGELA PROSTAMO, gazetted 16 November 1961. Three named Brisbane Prostamo with street addresses and exact dates — new to this archive, and untested against the line.

source: Trove — Prostamo before 1954
scope: The same keyword against the digitised Queensland newspapers, and PROSTAMO + funeral.
result: NEGATIVE. Not one Prostamo appears in a digitised Australian newspaper before 1961, and Domenica Prostamo's death on 3 May 1928 produced no notice that Trove holds. Weak evidence on its own — ordinary families rarely reach print — but it means the Brisbane newspapers will not date this family's arrival.

source: Trove — Melluso at Brisbane
scope: Keyword MELLUSO Brisbane.
result: Four results, all incidental: a 1964 Telegraph court list, a 1967 naturalisation gazette in which the name appears only in the surrounding column, and Commonwealth Savings Bank trustee notices of 1972. Nothing that touches Caterina Melluso or her father Leone.

source: Find a Grave — Prostamo and Melluso across Australia
scope: Both surnames searched nationally, not just at Nudgee.
result: SIX PROSTAMO AND FIVE MELLUSO, and NOT ONE AT NUDGEE, where every Australian Mazza in this archive is buried. Domenico Francesco Prostamo (1931-2025) and Maria Assunta Prostamo (1936-1991) lie in adjoining plots 608 and 607 at Mount Gravatt, Brisbane; Angela Majda Prostamo (1937-2016) at Nerang; and Rocco (1925-2004) and Francesca (1933-2018) Prostamo at Glenroy in MELBOURNE — a branch this archive did not know existed. Gregorio Melluso (1904-1971) is at Mareeba in the far north, Section 4 Catholic, Row I, Plot 10.

source: Queensland BDM — the historical index, by download
scope: The registrar's own downloadSearch endpoint returns the full result set as CSV, which makes an exact-surname sweep of births 1829-1926, marriages 1829-1951 and deaths 1829-1996 a single request per name. Prostamo, Postamo, Melluso, Limardo, Borello, Polistena.
result: One Prostamo in the whole index: Maria Assunta, died 27 October 1991, born 1936, parents Gregorio Melluso and Carmela Maria Borello. One Melluso: Gregorio, died 30 September 1971, parents Gennaro Melluso and Maria Limardo. Postamo, Limardo and Polistena return nothing at all. The eleven Borello are one Piedmontese household and not hers.

source: The Mount Gravatt burial records
scope: Brisbane City Council's cemetery search covers Mount Gravatt as the Nudgee endpoint covers Nudgee.
result: Plots 607 and 608 are known. The adjoining plots on either side are not, and at Nudgee it was the neighbouring plots that joined families to each other.

source: Antenati — Briatico, Matrimoni 1840-1849 and 1853
scope: Every page of every volume read by cropping the parroco's certificate box, which names both spouses, and montaging them.
result: THE MARRIAGE WAS FOUND. Briatico 1849 ATTO 1, 14 June: DOMENICO PROSTAMO marries GIOVANNA VENTRICE. Thirteen years of Briatico marriages were read to reach it — 1840 to 1848 hold no Prostamo at all, and neither do 1850, 1851, 1852 or 1854, read earlier. The act names ANTONINO PROSTAMO and MARIA FRAGALÀ, and says Domenico was born at PIZZO.

source: Antenati — Pizzo, the registers
scope: Domenico Prostamo was born at Pizzo about 1813; his mother Maria Fragalà was still living there in 1849; and the family tree puts his grandfather Pasquale's death at Pizzo on 4 January 1829.
result: ANSWERED, AND IT IS A WALL. Pizzo's holdings on Antenati contain ONLY the restaurazione fondo and BEGIN IN 1823 — tested on 1812, 1814, 1818 and 1822, all empty, and on 1823, which returns four volumes. Pasquale Prostamo's death act of January 1829 was read. Domenico Prostamo's birth act of 1814 and Antonino Prostamo's marriage cannot be opened at all.

source: Antenati — Briatico, Matrimoni allegati 1849
scope: The processetti filed with atto 1 of 1849.
result: DONE THE SAME DAY. The bundle is an_ua37921205 (Matrimoni processetti 1849-1854, container LDnmr1B) and its first file is Domenico Prostamo's. It gave Antonino Prostamo's death in the 1837 cholera register, a certified copy of Pasquale's death act filed as the groom's avo paterno, Domenico's own birth extract under the name ANTONIO, the atto di notorieta reconciling the two names, and two Ventrice death extracts.

source: Antenati — Potenzoni, in hindsight
scope: Opened on the reasoning that three Prostamo-free years of Briatico births meant the family was in the frazione.
result: THE REASONING WAS WRONG AND THE NEGATIVE WAS RIGHT. They were not at Potenzoni either; they were at Pizzo. Recorded because the mistake is instructive: an absence was read as evidence for a specific alternative rather than as evidence of absence, and the right move would have been to find a document that says where they were — which is what the marriage act eventually did. The Potenzoni mapping is kept; it is good work on a comune this family does not appear to belong to.

source: Antenati — Pizzo, Morti 1829

source: Antenati — Archivio di Stato di Messina, whole province
scope: Does civil registration at Messina reach back to Michele Donato's birth about 1814, and to his parents' marriage before it? Year-by-year probes of the province: 1815, 1819, 1820, 1821, 1825, 1840.
result: NO, AND THE WALL IS EXACT. 1815 returns nothing. 1819 returns nothing. 1820 returns 366 volumes across seventeen comuni, 1821 more, 1840 five hundred and ten. CIVIL REGISTRATION IN THE PROVINCE OF MESSINA BEGINS IN 1820 — six years after Michele Donato was born there, and later still than his parents' marriage. Sicily had no Napoleonic period, so it has no «Stato civile napoleonico»: the series starts with the restoration, and starts late. So CANDELORO DONATO IS WHERE THE SCILLA LINE STOPS in the civil registers, exactly as Pasquale Prostamo is where the Calabrian one does. Anything earlier is a PARISH record, in the Archdiocese of Messina, and not on Antenati. AND A SECOND WALL BEHIND THE FIRST: the comune of MESSINA ITSELF appears in none of the years read — not 1820, not 1840 — although the archive's series list claims 1069 volumes for it. Messina city was destroyed by the earthquake of 28 December 1908, which killed some eighty thousand people and took much of its civil archive with it. That is to be confirmed rather than assumed, but it means the city is the worst-served comune in its own province and the Donato birth may be unreachable by any route.

source: Brisbane City Council cemeteries — the whole register, by API
scope: All nine Council cemeteries and crematoria — Mount Gravatt, Toowong, Pinnaroo Lawn, Balmoral, Hemmant, Lutwyche, South Brisbane and the rest, 360,000 records. Searched: Mazza, Prostamo, Polistena, Arena, Donato, Melluso, Nicotra, Crupi, Cavallaro.
result: THE ENDPOINT, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: Council's search moved to «EverAfter», and behind it is clean JSON needing no login — GET https://brisbane.discovereverafter.com/api/deceased-search?name=SURNAME&country=&facility_id=&order_by=relevance&sort=desc . It returns forename, middlename, surname, date of birth, date of death, age, date of burial or cremation, and the cemetery. The match is FUZZY -- a search for Mazza returns Mazzaracca, Mazzaglia and Mazzaroli -- so filter on the surname yourself. FOUR NAMES RETURN NOTHING AT ALL across every Council cemetery: POLISTENA, MELLUSO, NICOTRA and CRUPI. That is not a failure, it is the shape of the family: they were Catholic and they are at NUDGEE, which the Archdiocese runs and Council does not list. WHAT IT CORRECTED: Domenico Francesco Prostamo's birth, recorded here as 1931, is 18 OCTOBER 1930 in Council's own record -- which agrees with the family tree and makes him ninety-four when he died in January 2025, not ninety-three. WHAT IT ADDED, AS LEADS AND NOT JOINS: MARIO MAZZA (1921-2015) and MARIA MAZZA (1931-2014) share plot Mon 3H 104 at Mount Gravatt, which in these registers means a married pair -- and neither is in Michael's export. AND AT PINNAROO LAWN, A DONATO FAMILY CARRYING THIS LINE'S TWO RAREST NAMES: «Gregory CANDELORO Donato» (1941-2025), «Donato CENDELORD» (d. 1968 at 52), «Donato ANNUNZIATO» (d. 1954 at 66), with a Rocco and a Concetta beside them. Candeloro is the name of the Scilla grandfather born about 1783 and of his grandson born 1847; Annunziata is Nunziata Sofi's. THE EXPORT CONTAINS NO CANDELORO AT ALL. This is exactly the shape of a join this archive has got wrong four times, so it is written down as a lead and nothing more. The Queensland death index names parents and would settle both.

source: Antenati — the Briatico processetti, mapped as a series
scope: Which years exist, which comuni they cover, and how they are arranged. Probed 1820, 1822, 1824, 1826, 1828, 1830, 1840, 1845, 1850.
result: THEY EXIST FOR MOST YEARS, AND THE SERIES IS NOT ONE COMUNE. Briatico returns TWO OR THREE separate processetti arks for the same year, and they are DIFFERENT COMUNI in the same circondario -- 1826 gives Briatico (an_ua37920142, 59 images) and SCICONI (an_ua37929531, 52 images); 1828 gives three plus a CONIDONI bundle covering 1828-1851 (an_ua37920221, 318 images). Read the manifest label before assuming which town a bundle belongs to. Years found: 1824 (an_ua37920082, 107 images), 1826, 1828, 1830, 1840, 1845, 1850. NOT 1820 and NOT 1822. AND THEY ARE ARRANGED DIFFERENTLY FROM SCILLA'S, which matters for what a search costs. Scilla's bundles are PER-MARRIAGE FASCICOLI, each opening with a cover sheet that names both spouses and indexes its own contents -- so the right file is found by reading covers. BRIATICO'S 1826 BUNDLE HAS NO COVER SHEETS AT ALL: it is a continuous run of loose notificazioni and certificates, «PARTE II», with the spouses' names in the body of each. SO THE ROUTE IN IS THE MARRIAGE REGISTER FIRST. Get the act number from the Briatico Matrimoni volume, then find the corresponding papers. Reading the bundle cold means reading every page. The target that prompted this: GIUSEPPE VENTRICE x CATERINA CICHELLO, married before mid-1827 -- their daughter Giovanna was born 23 June 1828. Their bundle would carry Giuseppe's own birth act (about 1795), Caterina Cichello's, HER PARENTS, and very possibly the death of PAOLO VENTRICE, which would reach a generation this archive has only as a name. NOT YET FOUND.

source: FamilySearch — UNBLOCKED after five days, and what it actually holds
scope: Retried after the site-wide Error 15 that named the proxy IP and blocked it from the day this archive was built. Searched Prostamo, Francesco Prostamo and Rosario Mazza.
result: IT WORKS, AND IT NEEDS NO LOGIN. The index returns names, exact dates, places AND BOTH PARENTS on the results page itself. The surname match is fuzzy -- «Prostamo» returns Prada, Pretta, Pretto and Preiti -- so add `q.surname.exact=on`, which cuts 1,335 results to 26. THE COLLECTION THAT MATTERS FOR THE CALABRIAN LINE: «Italy, Vibo Valentia, Vibo Valentia, Civil Registration (TRIBUNALE), 1861-1910» -- the COURT copy, which runs to 1910 where Antenati's comune copies stop at 1900. BUT NOT FOR BRIATICO. Twenty-six exact Prostamo births 1896-1912 are indexed and every one of them is MILETO, COMPARNI, SAN GIOVANNI or PIZZO. Not one is Briatico. FRANCESSCO PROSTAMO, BORN 16 NOVEMBER 1900 AT BRIATICO, IS NOT IN THE INDEX -- so Briatico's 1900-1910 volumes are either unindexed browse-only images here or absent, and that hope, which has sat in the queue since 10 September, is not a quick one after all. PIZZO IS INDEXED, which is worth knowing given the Prostamo are a Pizzo family: Giorgio Prostamo d. 1903 and Anna Prostamo d. 1899, both of Antonino/Antonio and Angela Conde. Too late for the spine but the same town. AND ONE THING THAT REFINES TODAY'S MESSINA FINDING. FamilySearch carries «Italy, MESSINA, Civil Registration (STATE ARCHIVE), 1820-1865». That CONFIRMS INDEPENDENTLY that Sicilian registration begins in 1820 -- and it softens the second wall: Messina's records for 1820-65 SURVIVE and are filmed, even though the comune of Messina appeared in no Antenati year probed. The earthquake of 1908 did not take everything. It does NOT move the first wall: Michele Donato was born about 1814, still six years early.

source: Antenati — Briatico marriages 1822 to 1827, read complete
scope: GIUSEPPE VENTRICE x CATERINA CICHELLO, whose daughter Giovanna was born 23 June 1828, so the marriage must precede it. Six whole years read from the annual Tavole: 1822, 1823, 1824, 1825, 1826, 1827.
result: NEGATIVE, AND FIRM. TWENTY-FOUR MARRIAGES IN SIX YEARS AND NOT ONE VENTRICE. 1822 had five. 1823 had five, 1824 four, 1825 four or five, 1826 five, AND 1827 HAD NONE AT ALL -- its Tavola is ruled and completely empty. WHERE TO LOOK NEXT, and the negative points at it: Giuseppe Ventrice DIED at Briatico in 1831, but his father DOMENICO VENTRICE died at ZAMBRONE in 1815. The family was a Zambrone family that moved. The marriage is most likely at ZAMBRONE, or earlier than 1823 at Briatico, or Giovanna was not the first child. AND A METHOD FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE NEGATIVE. BRIATICO'S MARRIAGE VOLUMES ARE TINY AND EVERY ONE CARRIES AN ANNUAL TAVOLA THAT NAMES BOTH SETS OF PARENTS. The volumes run six to thirteen images; the Tavola is the LAST image or the one before it, ruled for «Nomi e cognomi dei Sposi | PATRIA | NOMI E COGNOMI DE' GENITORI | Giorno della celebrazione». So a whole year of Briatico marriages, with four parents for every couple, costs ONE IMAGE. The series runs 1816 to 1858 and the arks are sequential -- ark(Y) = an_ua87654 + (Y - 1840), which is CONFIRMED BACKWARDS as well: 1824 is an_ua87638, 1827 is an_ua87641. The entire Briatico marriage series could be swept for about forty images. Nothing else in this archive is that cheap. AND THE TAVOLA CONVENTION STARTS SOMEWHERE AROUND 1822: the volumes for 1816 and 1817 end on ACTS, not an index, so those years must be read act by act. The remaining window for this marriage is therefore 1816-1821 at Briatico -- about seventy images, all downloadable, none indexed -- or Zambrone. Containers found: 1816 5VKDrmE, 1817 5dZbKXn, 1818 wRGR73a, 1819 Lydrvn1, 1820 wlGnjVD, 1821 w68pynN, 1822 wbrz4Vg, 1823 w99lEay, 1824 wXrR28W, 1825 LNjzb4J, 1826 0JbOyEd, 1827 0A4Xgj9.

source: Antenati — the Zambrone marriage book, first fifty images (1811-1830)
scope: GIUSEPPE VENTRICE x CATERINA CICHELLO, after Briatico 1822-27 came back negative. Zambrone Matrimoni 1811-1858, an_ua37928578, container wWyoZJ2, 253 images. Annual Tavole read complete for 1822, 1824 and 1826; the acts of the other years not yet read.
result: NOT FOUND YET, BUT THE FAMILY IS THERE, WHICH IS WHAT THE BRIATICO NEGATIVE PREDICTED. TAVOLE READ COMPLETE: 1822 (five marriages -- Scarpato x Sambiase, Coglia x Adamo, Pungitori x Pietrapaolo, Trillo x Colica, Trillo x Ferraro) and 1824 (three -- Piatto x Viggo, Trillo x Pellegrino, Sorrentino x Colica). NO VENTRICE IN EITHER. AND A VENTRICE AT LAST, in the Tavola at image 40: «VINCENZO SORRENTINO x SERAFINA VENTRICE», celebrated a 9 Agosto. HER FATHER READS AS FRANCESCO -- so a different branch from Domenico Ventrice's, and not the couple wanted. THE YEAR IS NOW SETTLED: 1826. Each year in this volume ends on UNUSED BLANK PRINTED FORMS before its Tavola -- image 34 is a blank 1825 form, image 39 a blank 1826 form -- and the Tavola at image 40 follows the 1826 blanks. So SORRENTINO x SERAFINA VENTRICE WERE MARRIED AT ZAMBRONE ON 9 AUGUST 1826, and 1826's three marriages hold no Giuseppe Ventrice. ONE CAUTION REMAINS: the parents' column is cramped and faded, so FRANCESCO -- which would make Serafina a different branch from Domenico Ventrice's -- is a reading and not a certainty. An act of 23 January 1830 at image 50 also names a Vincenzo Sorrentino «sposo di Serafina Ventrice», which may be the same couple's civil promise or may be a second entry -- unresolved. STRUCTURE, which makes the rest cheap: each year is a printed title page, then acts one to an opening, then an annual TAVOLA naming BOTH SETS OF PARENTS. Located so far -- image 13 Tavola 1822, image 18 a BLANK 1823 form, image 27 Tavola 1824, image 28 title 1825, image 35 title 1826, image 40 a Tavola, image 48 a Tavola, image 49 title 1830. SO FOUR YEARS ARE NOW CLEAR -- 1822, 1824, 1826 at Zambrone, on top of Briatico 1822-1827 -- AND THE WINDOW IS 1811-1821, 1823, 1825 AND 1827. Giuseppe Ventrice was born about 1795, so 1818-1825 is where to look first. All fifty images are downloaded.

source: Antenati — Zambrone Matrimoni 1824, atto 2. FOUND.
scope: GIUSEPPE VENTRICE x CATERINA CICHELLO, hunted across Briatico 1822-1827 and Zambrone 1822-1826 before this.
result: FOUND, ON 2 MARCH 1824 AT ZAMBRONE, and it was three images from where the sweep had already reached. The reason it took so long is worth recording: THE TAVOLE IN THIS VOLUME LEAVE THEIR YEAR BLANK. The printed header reads «nell'anno ___» and nobody filled it in, so the year has to be deduced from position -- and I deduced it wrong, calling the Tavola at image 27 «1824» when its three couples are the acts of 1823. Reading the ACTS, which carry «L'Anno mille ottocentoventiquattro» in print, settled it in one look. RULE: IN THIS SERIES, TRUST THE ACTS FOR THE YEAR AND THE TAVOLA ONLY FOR THE NAMES. What the act gives is on the plate and in the corrections: Caterina Cichello's parents FRANCESCO CICHELLO and VITTORIA MOLLO, a couple entirely new to this archive; Giuseppe's birthplace S. COSTANTINO; all four parents already dead by 1824; and a direct contradiction of the 1849 chancery copy over whether Domenico Ventrice's wife was ANNA FAMA or ANNA MAROPOLI.

source: Antenati — Zambrone Morti 1811-1839, opened. THE GAP IS REAL AND NOW EXACT.
scope: Whether Zambrone's deaths really are missing 1813-1821 — a wall this archive has published for days without ever opening the volume. Zambrone Morti 1811-1839, an_ua37932358, container w9dp62r, 234 images.
result: THE WALL IS REAL, AND IT IS NOT AN INFERENCE ANY MORE. The volume runs 1811 (images 1-24), then 1812, which ENDS WITH ITS OWN DEATH TAVOLA at images 37-38, then a printed title page at image 39 — AND THEN IMAGE 40 IS 1822. Acts 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 of 1822 run from image 40 to image 45. SO THE REGISTER JUMPS FROM THE END OF 1812 STRAIGHT TO 1822 AND THE YEARS 1813 TO 1821 ARE PHYSICALLY ABSENT. Nine years, and this archive had them right. WHAT THAT COSTS: DOMENICO VENTRICE DIED 13 JANUARY 1815, squarely inside the gap. His original death act is NOT in this volume, so the ANNA FAMA against ANNA MAROPOLI question CANNOT be settled from Zambrone's own register. BUT THE SURNAME IS CORROBORATED ANYWAY, and from an unexpected direction: the 1822 death Tavola names a «fu Franc.co e Dom.ca MAROPOLI» as the parents of a Francesca Pungitori. MAROPOLI IS A REAL ZAMBRONE SURNAME OF EXACTLY THIS PERIOD, which is what a reading of «della fu Anna Maropoli» needed and did not have. It does not prove the 1849 copy wrong; it removes the objection that the name looked invented. AND THE VOLUME IS CHEAP TO SWEEP: EVERY YEAR ENDS WITH AN ANNUAL TAVOLA ruled for «Nomi e Cognomi dei Morti | Patria | Professione | NOMI E COGNOMI DE' GENITORI | Giorno della Morte». 1812's is at image 37, 1822's at image 51. One image a year, with the parents of every person who died. 1822 READ COMPLETE: seven deaths, and NEITHER Francesco Cichello NOR Vittoria Mollo is among them — though a MARIA Mollo died on 27 May 1822.

source: Antenati — Zambrone death Tavole 1822, 1823 and 1824, read complete
scope: FRANCESCO CICHELLO and VITTORIA MOLLO, both already dead when their daughter married on 2 March 1824 — so their deaths fall somewhere before that. And ANNA MAROPOLI, Giuseppe Ventrice's mother, also «la fu» by 1824. Zambrone Morti 1811-1839: Tavola 1822 at image 51, 1823 at image 65, 1824 at image 78.
result: NEGATIVE FOR ALL THREE, AND THE NEGATIVE POINTS SOMEWHERE USEFUL. The three annual death Tavole name everyone who died at Zambrone in 1822, 1823 and 1824, WITH THEIR PARENTS -- and NEITHER FRANCESCO CICHELLO NOR VITTORIA MOLLO IS AMONG THEM. Nor is Anna Maropoli. SO ALL THREE ALMOST CERTAINLY DIED IN THE NINE MISSING YEARS, 1813-1821 -- the same gap that hides Domenico Ventrice's act of January 1815. Four people this archive wants, behind one gap. That makes the SECOND COPY of the register (work list row 59) the single most valuable lead left on the Calabrian side. WHAT THE SWEEP DID SETTLE: MAROPOLI IS UNMISTAKABLY A ZAMBRONE SURNAME. It appears TWICE more in these three years -- «fu Franc.co e Dom.ca MAROPOLI» as parents in the 1822 Tavola, and GIUSEPPE MAROPOLI himself, an infant, dead 23 March 1824, son of Antonio and Marianna Colia. Two independent attestations inside two years. The reading «della fu Anna Maropoli» on the 1824 marriage act no longer needs defending as a reading; what remains open is only which of two documents is right. AND A PLACE WORTH NOTING: the 1824 Tavola's first entry is FRANCESCA CAPIGRELLI OF S. COSTANTINO -- the same S. Costantino where Giuseppe Ventrice was born. Zambrone's register carries S. Costantino people, so the two towns shared a population and the Ventrice move was a short one. MOLLO AND CICHELLO ARE BOTH LOCAL: a Maria Mollo died in 1822, a Marianna Mollo and an Anna Cichello in 1823, a Domenica Mollo appears as a parent in 1824. Neither surname is rare here, which is worth remembering before any join is made on one.

source: FamilySearch catalogue — attempted, and it was down
scope: The second copy of Zambrone's civil registers for 1813-1821, the nine years missing from the Antenati volume.
result: NOT RULED OUT -- NOT CHECKED. FamilySearch's catalogue returned «Something Went Wrong» for every query on 15 September. Its JSON endpoint at /service/search/catalog/search is alive and validates query terms -- `q.title`, `q.subject` and `q.place` are accepted where `q.text`, `q.keyword` and `q.anyPlace` are rejected -- but `q.place=Zambrone` IGNORES the value and returns two million hits, so it is useless without a place ID. RETRY LATER; this is a service outage and not a negative. WHAT THE ATTEMPT DID PRODUCE, by making me check the premise instead: THE VOLUME ANTENATI HOLDS IS THE COURT'S COPY, NOT THE COMUNE'S. Its manifest says «Archivio di Stato di Catanzaro > Stato civile napoleonico > Zambrone > 1811-1839», and under the Napoleonic and Bourbon codes every act was written TWICE -- one register for the comune, one for the tribunale, the tribunale's going to the Archivio di Stato. SO THE NINE YEARS ARE MISSING FROM ONE OF TWO COPIES, and the other may still be at the COMUNE DI ZAMBRONE. That is supported by the act having existed in 1849, when the chancery certified a copy of Domenico Ventrice's 1815 death for a marriage at Briatico -- something was still being copied from, thirty-four years on. It makes the next step a LETTER to the comune rather than another search, and it is the only route to four people: Domenico Ventrice, Anna Maropoli, Francesco Cichello and Vittoria Mollo.

source: Queensland BDM — swept by surname for Donato, Mazza and Crupi
scope: Testing the two Brisbane leads found in the council cemeteries — the Pinnaroo Donato carrying CANDELORO, and Mario and Maria Mazza of Mount Gravatt — and sweeping the surname sets properly rather than by targeted lookup. The endpoint 403s to curl and must be fetched from the site's own origin in the browser.
result: THREE RESULTS, AND ONE OF THEM IS A FAMILY NOBODY HERE KNEW ABOUT. CRUPI -- ANGELA CRUPI HAD AT LEAST THREE BROTHERS IN QUEENSLAND. Her own death registration of 1973 names FRANCESCO CRUPI and MARIA VECCHIO. So do THREE MORE: PIETRO CRUPI (d. 18 July 1961), ANTONINO CRUPI (d. 15 April 1982) and MARIO CRUPI (d. 17 September 1989). Four siblings, one parent-pair, and this archive knew one of them. Two of the brothers also have Queensland marriages in 1940. DONATO -- THE PINNAROO FAMILY IS FULLY DOCUMENTED AND IS NOT DEMONSTRABLY OURS. ANNUNZIATO DONATO and CONCETTA BRIGANTI had five children registered in Queensland: Rocco 1912, Concetto 1913, Peppino 1914, CANDELORO 1915 and Nunzio 1917, and the deaths of four of them repeat the same parents. AND ANNUNZIATO'S OWN DEATH OF 28 FEBRUARY 1954 NAMES HIS PARENTS: ROCCO DONATO and CONCETTA ROMANO. NOT Michele Donato and Maria Sofi. So the Candeloro at Pinnaroo is a grandson of a ROCCO Donato, not of this archive's line. THE NAMES REMAIN SUGGESTIVE AND THAT IS ALL THEY ARE: Candeloro, Annunziato, Rocco, Nunzio and Concetto are precisely the Scilla Donato naming pool, and CONCETTA ROMANO carries a surname this archive has already met at Scilla in Giovanni Polistena's mother. A cousin line is plausible. A DOCUMENTED LINK IS ABSENT, and this is exactly the join this archive has got wrong four times. MAZZA -- THE MOUNT GRAVATT PAIR CANNOT BE TESTED HERE AT ALL. Queensland's public death index stops at 1996 and MARIO MAZZA DIED IN 2015, MARIA MAZZA IN 2014. The Mario Mazza who appears in the index died in 1986 and is a different man, son of Rosario Mazza and Rosa Grasso. The lead is neither confirmed nor refuted; it is out of the index's reach. The sweep also re-confirmed five registrations this archive already held -- Maria Nicotra 1963, Mary Rosa Mazza 1968, Rosario Mazza 1986, Michele Mazza 1926 and Angela Crupi 1973 -- with the same parents each time.

source: Queensland BDM — the rest of the surnames swept
scope: Prostamo, Polistena, Melluso, Nicotra, Anile, Barbuto and Arena, by exact surname, births marriages and deaths.
result: MOSTLY EMPTY, AND THE EMPTINESS IS INFORMATIVE. POLISTENA RETURNS NOTHING AT ALL, and so does ANILE. That is not a gap in the family, it is the shape of the index: births stop in 1926, marriages in 1951, deaths in 1996, and the Polistena reached Brisbane in 1949. They arrived too late to be born or married into it and have mostly died too late to be in it. PROSTAMO RETURNS EXACTLY ONE RECORD in the entire Queensland index -- Maria Assunta, 1991 -- for a family with a dozen people in Brisbane. Same reason. ARENA RETURNS SEVENTY-FIVE AND NONE OF THEM IS OURS: Byrne, Kerby, Pollard, Timothy Leo, Cornelius Joseph, Alphonso James -- an IRISH-AUSTRALIAN Arena family entirely unrelated to Scilla. A surname sweep without a parent check would have produced a dozen false joins here. NICOTRA returns eighteen, of which ONE is ours -- Maria Nicotra, 1963, already held. The rest are a Catania Nicotra cluster around Maccarone, Patane and Scalia. BARBUTO returns two, neither ours. AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EXPECTATION: the Melluso and Prostamo registrations I treated as finds were ALREADY IN data/qld-bdm.tsv, recorded by an earlier session with better analysis than mine -- including that LIMARDO is a Potenzoni surname from the 1818 birth index. What was actually missing was that GENNARO MELLUSO, MARIA LIMARDO and CARMELA MARIA BORELLO had never become PEOPLE. They are now. The lesson is about this archive, not about Queensland: facts recorded in one file do not reach the reader until they are surfaced in another.

source: FamilySearch — Australian records for Prostamo
scope: Looking for AUSTRALIAN ELECTORAL ROLLS, promoted to the primary instrument after Queensland BDM proved unable to see a family that arrived in 1949.
result: NO ELECTORAL ROLLS THERE. FamilySearch's Australian holdings for this surname are Petty Sessions registers, Find a Grave and nothing else -- the rolls are on Ancestry, which is paid, and at the National Library. So row 62 still needs a source and this was not it. TWO THINGS THE SEARCH DID GIVE. FIRST, A PLACE AND A DATE FOR ROCCO PROSTAMO. «Australia, Victoria, Petty Sessions Registers, 1858-1985» indexes a PROSTAMO at NORTHCOTE between November 1956 and June 1957, and at HEIDELBERG between December 1957 and June 1958 -- both Melbourne. The index garbles the given name as «Ricco» and «Rono», which is this data's usual treatment of ROCCO. It fits: Rocco Prostamo, born 28 January 1925, is buried at NORTHERN MEMORIAL PARK, GLENROY, in the same city. WHAT THE ENTRIES CONCERN IS NOT STATED IN THE INDEX AND HAS NOT BEEN READ -- petty sessions covered licences, debts, permits and minor matters alike -- so this is recorded as a PLACE AND A DATE and nothing more. It should not be characterised further without reading the register itself. SECOND, A CAUTION ABOUT FIND A GRAVE. It indexes FRANCESCA PROSTAMO, born 18 September 1933 and died 11 February 2018, at TWO DIFFERENT CEMETERIES ON TWO CONTINENTS -- «Northern Memorial Park, Glenroy, Victoria» and «Northern Cemetery, Barnesville, Belmont County, OHIO». Same dates, same name, one person. The two cemeteries share the word NORTHERN and that is almost certainly the whole explanation. This archive uses the Victorian one, because she landed at Fremantle in 1957 and Rocco is buried in the same Melbourne ground. A Find a Grave hit is not a burial until the cemetery agrees.

source: Antenati — San Costantino Calabro, mapped for the first time
scope: The town named in Giuseppe Ventrice's marriage act of 1824 as his birthplace — «nato in S. Costantino» — and never once queried by this archive.
result: IT EXISTS, IT IS LARGE, AND IT REACHES BACK FURTHER THAN ZAMBRONE'S SURVIVING DEATHS. 205 volumes, 1810 to 1912, including NATI 1812-1824 and 1813-1860, MORTI 1813-1827, 1828-1837 and 1838-1849, MATRIMONI 1813-1832, and FORTY-EIGHT volumes of MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A NEW TOWN USUALLY WOULD: ZAMBRONE'S DEATH REGISTER IS MISSING 1813-1821, and four people this archive wants died inside that gap. SAN COSTANTINO'S MORTI 1813-1827 COVERS EXACTLY THOSE YEARS. If ANNA MAROPOLI -- Giuseppe Ventrice's mother, «la fu» by March 1824 -- died in her husband's own town rather than at Zambrone, HER ACT SURVIVES. The gap may be walkable round rather than through. GIUSEPPE'S OWN BIRTH IS STILL OUT OF REACH: he was about 1790 and the registers begin in 1810. AND THE USUAL TRAP, MET AGAIN: the volume labelled «San Costantino 1813-1827» (an_ua37932372, container wRDnEp4, 325 images) IS NOT ONE COMUNE. Image 12 is San Costantino; images 24 and 40 are FRANCICA. Read the comune line on every act, not the series label. NOT YET SWEPT -- 325 mixed images, and the year structure has not been mapped.

source: Antenati — Pizzo, the whole series listed
scope: Everything Antenati holds for Pizzo, to see what is reachable above and around the Prostamo wall.
result: 751 VOLUMES, AND THE WALL IS CONFIRMED FROM THE SERIES ITSELF: the earliest is 1823, exactly as this archive has said. WHAT IS REACHABLE: Nati from 1823, Morti from 1823, Matrimoni 1823-1829, and THIRTY-FOUR VOLUMES OF MATRIMONI PROCESSETTI. MARIA FRAGALA was alive at Pizzo in June 1849 and is the one person on this line whose death falls INSIDE the surviving run. ANTONINO PROSTAMO x MARIA FRAGALA married about 1810-13 -- their son was born April 1814 -- which is ten years before the register starts, so the marriage is pre-civil like the rest. The 1837 cholera register remains the exception: indexed to act 325 and not digitised.

source: Brisbane cemeteries — the three Crupi brothers, both registers
scope: PIETRO (d. 1961), ANTONINO (d. 1982) and MARIO CRUPI (d. 1989), found today in the Queensland death index as brothers of Angela Crupi. Searched Brisbane City Council's nine cemeteries and the Catholic Archdiocese's nine, including wildcard variants Crup%, Crupi% and Cruppi.
result: NOT IN EITHER REGISTER. Council returns ZERO Crupi across all nine of its cemeteries and crematoria. The Catholic register returns EXACTLY ONE, and it is none of them: VENERO CRUPI, born 14 October 1935, died 4 December 2023, interred at NUDGEE on 13 December 2023, plot LA-3299. SO THE THREE BROTHERS ARE BURIED SOMEWHERE NEITHER REGISTER COVERS -- outside Brisbane, or cremated privately, or in a ground held by neither the council nor the Archdiocese. Their death registrations carry no C country code, so they died in the Brisbane district, which makes the absence odder rather than less. VENERO CRUPI IS A LEAD AND IS LEFT AS ONE. Venero is a Catania name and Angela Crupi was born at Catania in 1900, so he fits the family's origin exactly -- and fitting an origin is not a descent. He died in December 2023, well within living memory, and the people who could confirm him are alive. This is a question for Michael, not for an index.

source: Findmypast — Australia Electoral Rolls, the whole Mazza and Prostamo sweep
scope: Every Mazza and every Prostamo in Findmypast's Australia Electoral Rolls, sorted to bring all Queensland rows onto the first page, with transcripts read for the six that could be this family.
result: SIX TRANSCRIPTS AND ONE HARD LIMIT. FOUND: SEBASTIANO MAZZA, builder's labourer, Progress Road, WACOL, sub-district Inala, 1959 -- Michael Mazza's grandfather, ten years after landing, in the post-war migrant belt. ROSARIO MAZZA, shopkeeper, and ANGELA MAZZA, home duties, at 225 LEICHHARDT STREET, Brisbane city, 1959, on consecutive roll numbers 1844 and 1845, which is one household; Rosario is Sebastiano's brother and Angela is very probably Angela Cupo. ROSARIO SALVATORE MAZZA, shop assistant, 191 Given Terrace, PADDINGTON, 1949 -- the same man a decade earlier, carrying his father Salvatore's name. ANDREA MAZZA, timber cutter at Cardwell in the TULLY sub-district, where Rosario's daughter Carmela was born in 1926, unidentified and left as a lead. ANTONIO MAZZA, tobacco grower at Yelarbon, recorded to close him off. NOTHING FOR DOMENICA PROSTAMO under either name, and ZERO PROSTAMO in all of Australia. THE LIMIT: Findmypast holds only eight Queensland commonwealth years and the last is 1959, so for a family that arrived in 1949 there is ONE usable roll. The near-annual run this archive was promised is at the NLA and on Ancestry, not here.

source: NAA — the Ugolino Vivaldi manifest of 1 March 1951, read in full
scope: All 25 images of NAA K269, item 30133197: the Lloyd Triestino master list of incoming passengers for trip 2/51, and the Department of Immigration's schedule of alien passengers for debarkation at Fremantle. Searched for MAZZA, for PROSTAMO, and for any accompanying child.
result: IT DISPROVES THE IDENTIFICATION THIS ARCHIVE HAS CARRIED SINCE THE CROSSINGS WERE FIRST WORKED. ONE MAZZA aboard: «MAZZA Domenico», no. 476, Alien, bound for NARRACAN, VICTORIA. NO PROSTAMO aboard under any spelling -- the P sequence runs PRATICO', PREBIANCA, PRELL, POTH, PUGLISI with no gap. NO SECOND MAZZA, and the list names children individually, so a two-year-old Salvatore would have been on it. THE PORT COLUMN IS THE PROOF: unlabelled in the master list, but every -F- passenger appears in the separate Fremantle debarkation schedule and every -M- has a Victorian address, so F is Fremantle and M is Melbourne. MAZZA Domenico is -M- and he is ABSENT from the Fremantle schedule, which runs MARTINELLI straight to MERENDINO. DOMENICA PROSTAMO WAS GOING TO HER HUSBAND IN BRISBANE; this man landed at Melbourne for a Gippsland shire. The candidate is withdrawn and her March 1951 crossing is unknown again. THE INDEX COULD NEVER HAVE SHOWN THIS. It gave a name, a date and a ship; the manifest gave a destination and a port of debarkation, and those are what broke it.

source: NAA RecordSearch NameSearch — Mazza, Prostamo and the naturalisation files
scope: NameSearch by family name across all record categories for MAZZA (Sebastiano, Rosario, Domenica), PROSTAMO, and the whole immigration and naturalisation category for MAZZA.
result: THE BEST SINGLE HOUR OF AUSTRALIAN RESEARCH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD. FOUND: NAA J25 1971/1074, «Mazza, Sebastiano; wife Domenica [nee Prostamo]», Brisbane, 1950-1971 -- the naturalisation file the 1959 electoral roll proved must exist, naming both of them and her maiden name. NAA MP1103/1 Q8110, «Prisoner of War/Internee: Mazza, Rosario; Date of birth - 20 February 1899» -- ROSARIO MAZZA WAS INTERNED as an enemy alien, with a Queensland investigation file (BP242/1 Q21227) and a Civil Aliens Corps record (J1737) behind it. NAA A12508 31/1454 -- ANGELA CRUPI ARRIVED AT BRISBANE ON THE VIMINALE ON 7 DECEMBER 1937 with «Maria age 15; Carmela age 8», which gives her birth date as 20 December 1900 and puts this family in Australia a decade before anyone here thought. J25 1970/5500 -- Sebastiano Mazza NOMINATED Mario Napoli, born 1934, and his wife Maria nee Coco. TWO PROSTAMO BROTHERS CORROBORATED with the wives the tree already names: J25 1961/3716 «PROSTAMO, Antonino Giacomo and Angela [nee Tomsic]» and J25 1962/5930 «Prostamo, Domenico Francesco; wife Assunte Maria [nee Melluso]». THE CAUTION: an NAA item title is a FINDING AID, not a record that has been read. It is transcribed from the file and it is reliable, but nothing here has been opened -- all of it is paper, most of it at Brisbane, and J25 1971/1074 is «not yet examined» and needs an access request. AND ONE THING BREAKS: Carmela arrives aged EIGHT as an Italian alien, so she was not born at Tully in 1926.

source: NAA — Mario Crupi's aliens registration card, read in full
scope: NAA: D4028, CRUPI MARIO, item 9209611 — digitised, two sides, read. Found by sweeping the NAA name index for CRUPI, POLISTENA and ARENA.
result: THE MOST DETAILED DOCUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS ON ANY AUSTRALIAN MEMBER OF THIS FAMILY, and it is free and digitised. N.B.E. certificate Q30124. MARIO CRUPI, born 28 NOVEMBER 1905 at PIEDIMONTE, PROVINCE OF CATANIA. Cane cutter. Address Bemerside P.O., INGHAM. Entered Australia 13 JUNE 1928, PORT OF DEBARKATION BRISBANE. Five feet eight, brown eyes, black hair, heavy build; SCAR ON LEFT THIGH, WART ON RIGHT SIDE OF FACE. THE REVERSE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: «18.8.42 LOVEDAY INTERNMENT CAMP. 30/12/43 Released and entrained for Brisbane.» HE WAS INTERNED FOR SIXTEEN MONTHS. THAT IS TWO MEN IN THIS FAMILY INTERNED IN 1942 -- Rosario Mazza on his own dossier, and now his wife's brother. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS THE BIRTHPLACE. PIEDIMONTE IS THE MAZZA'S OWN TOWN. Rosario Mazza was born at Piedimonte Etneo in 1899 and married Angela Crupi, born about 1900 in the province of Catania -- and here is her brother, born at Piedimonte Etneo in 1905. THE CRUPI AND THE MAZZA CAME FROM THE SAME VILLAGE, which this archive did not know and which is how these marriages were made. THE IDENTIFICATION IS STRONG AND IS NOT PROVED: the card names no parents. It rests on the surname, the birthplace, the north Queensland cane districts where the Crupi brothers appear on the electoral rolls, and the 1989 Queensland death of a Mario Crupi whose parents are Francesco Crupi and Maria Vecchio.

source: Antenati name index — every Arena death at Scilla, 1910-1943
scope: Antenati's «cerca per nome» index, cognome=Arena, localita=Scilla: 69 indexed persons, of whom 26 are the deceased and the rest appear as the parents and spouses named in those same acts.
result: THE INSTRUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN WORKING WITHOUT. Antenati NAME-INDEXES Scilla's death acts from about 1910 to 1943, with FATHER, MOTHER AND SPOUSE on each one, and it can be queried directly -- so a death that would have cost a volume list, a container lookup, a manifest fetch and an index read is now one search. THE THREE THAT MATTER. ROCCO ARENA, the New York emigrant, DIED AT SCILLA ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932: «Padre Francesco Antonio, Madre Serafina Arlotta, Coniuge Generosa Costa», all three matching this archive exactly. GIOVANNI ARENA, his brother, DIED AT SCILLA ON 31 MARCH 1936, «Madre Serafina Arlotta, Coniuge Concetta Russo» -- he sailed to join Rocco in 1899 and he came home, which is why he baptised no child in New York. SERAFINA ARENA, born in Manhattan on 15 August 1898, DIED AT SCILLA ON 15 AUGUST 1912. AND A WHOLE HOUSEHOLD FALLS OUT AS A BY-PRODUCT: Orazio Arena and Giovanna Zirilli's children TERESA (d. 1913, wife of Pietro Bova), GIUSEPPE (d. 1922, husband of Fortunata Maria Pontillo), MARIA ANNUNZIATA (d. 1933, wife of Rocco Chirico) and ALESSANDRO ANTONIO (d. 1936, husband of Maria Antonia Lico) -- plus a DOMENICO ARENA (d. 1923) whose mother is MARIANTONIA MUSOLINO, which means Orazio married twice. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT AND WHAT IT PROVES: FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA and SERAFINA ARLOTTA are named repeatedly as parents but never as the deceased, so they did not die inside 1910-1943. The archive had already read the annual index for 1889-1896 and not found them. THEY DIED BETWEEN 1897 AND 1909 -- row 69 goes from forty-seven unread years to THIRTEEN. ALL TWENTY-SIX WRITTEN OUT, 20 SEPTEMBER, AND THE SUMMARY HAD BEEN HIDING THINGS. This row named eight of the twenty-six deceased and moved on. The answer to a question asked four days later -- whose son was the Filippo Arena of the 1904 act -- was in the other eighteen all along: FILIPPO ARENA, d. 17 March 1915, «Padre Giovanni Arena, Madre Natalina Longordo, Coniuge Clementina Furfari». The full twenty-six are now in scilla-reads, and they resolve the surname into AT LEAST SEVEN SCILLA HOUSEHOLDS. A SELECTIVE RECORD OF A COMPLETE SEARCH COSTS THE SEARCH TWICE. Where a query returns a bounded set, write the set down.

source: Antenati name index — Donato, Arlotta and Polistena deaths at Scilla
scope: Antenati's name index, localita=Scilla, for DONATO (11 deceased), ARLOTTA (24) and POLISTENA (25) — each act carrying father, mother and spouse.
result: FOUR WORK-LIST ROWS ANSWERED FROM ONE INSTRUMENT. ROW 70, CLOSED: MICHELE DONATO died at Scilla on 10 MAY 1936, «Padre Domenico, Madre Nunziata Sofi, Coniuge Maria Sofi». He was the last man on the Donato line whose end was unknown; he was fifty-two on the 1908 New Orleans manifest and lived another twenty-eight years after coming home. ROW 96 AND ROW 41, BOTH CLOSED BY ONE ACT: CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA died 19 OCTOBER 1924, «Padre GIUSEPPE, Madre ANNA PONTILLO, Coniuge GIOVANNA ROMANO». That gives the thinnest quarter TWO NEW ANCESTORS -- and it explains the archive's oldest unresolved conflict. The tree calls Giovanni Polistena's mother «Giovanna Pontillo»; three records already called her ROMANO; here is a fourth, and here is where the Pontillo came from -- IT IS HIS GRANDMOTHER'S SURNAME, one generation up, carried down onto the wrong woman. The tree's «Giuseppi Pontillo» is Camillo Antonio's own father GIUSEPPE POLISTENA. ROW 4, PREDICTION CONFIRMED: the row reasoned from naming custom that Domenico Donato and Nunziata Sofi should have a PASQUALE, for the maternal grandfather Pasquale Sofi. PASQUALE DONATO died 20 APRIL 1937 with both parents named. ROW 39, THREE SIBLINGS FOR SERAFINA ARLOTTA: DOMENICO (d. 14 March 1915), ANNA (d. 16 March 1915) and GIUSEPPE ANTONIO (d. 2 June 1918), all «Padre Giovanni Arlotta, Madre Maria Costa». Domenico and Anna died TWO DAYS APART, which is worth reading the acts for. AND ONE SMALL CORRECTION: Teressa Polistena died 5 JANUARY 1933, not 1934.

source: Antenati name index — what Scilla actually has indexed, and for which years
scope: The whole Scilla name index with no surname filter: 13,777 indexed persons. Read the year facet across its full span, then pulled every act for 1880, 1902 and 1909 to see what type they are.
result: IT IS DEATHS, AND ONLY DEATHS, AND THE ANSWER DEFLATES FOUR ROWS WHILE SHARPENING THEM. Every act in the index, across every year from 1880 to 1943, is an ATTO DI MORTE. There are NO BIRTHS and NO MARRIAGES in it. THE COVERAGE IS 1911 TO 1943, SOLIDLY -- between 279 and 704 indexed persons a year -- with only a SCATTER BEFORE THAT: four persons in 1880, one in 1885, and a handful each in 1902, 1905, 1906, 1908, 1909 and 1910. WHAT THAT COSTS. The marriage of Nunziata Donato and Giovanni Polistena about 1916 is NOT reachable by query and stays a volume read; so is Camillo Antonio Polistena's birth about 1835, and so are the Donato births of 1845-1860. THE HOPE THAT ONE QUERY WOULD ANSWER THEM IS GONE. WHAT IT GAINS. The window it does cover, 1911-1943, is exactly when the Italian relatives of this family's emigrants were dying, which is why it gave up Rocco Arena, his brother Giovanni, Michele Donato and Camillo Antonio Polistena in an afternoon. AND TWO CAUTIONS. «anno=» is the year parameter and it is control-tested -- anno=1880 returns 4, matching the facet exactly, while «estremoRemoto=» is silently ignored and returns all 13,777. AND THE PRE-1911 STRAGGLERS ARE NOT A BACK DOOR INTO THE MISSING VOLUMES: the two acts indexed under 1909 carry document arks an_ud16595370 and an_ud16595649, which fall INSIDE the ark ranges of the 1911 and 1912 volumes. They are 1909 deaths written into later registers, not a 1909 volume that browse cannot see. A NOTE ON SIZE: 13,777 indexed persons is not 13,777 deaths. Each act indexes the deceased plus two or three relatives, so the real figure is nearer a quarter of that.

source: Antenati name index — every Costa death at Scilla, 1880-1943
scope: Antenati's name index, cognome=Costa, localita=Scilla: 76 indexed persons, 18 of them the deceased.
result: IT CLOSED THE COUSIN QUESTION AND OPENED TWO GENERATIONS. GENEROSA COSTA, Rocco Arena's wife, DIED AT SCILLA ON 6 JUNE 1916 -- «Padre ANTONINO COSTA, Madre ANNA ARLOTTA, Coniuge ROCCO ARENA». She died sixteen years before her husband. HER FATHER'S OWN ACT IS HERE TOO: ANTONIO COSTA, died 1 JUNE 1915, «Padre LORENZO COSTA, Madre GENEROSA POLISTENA» -- TWO NEW ANCESTORS on a line that stopped dead at him, and the reason for his daughter's name, since the first daughter takes the paternal grandmother's. IT ALSO PUTS A POLISTENA INSIDE THE COSTA LINE a generation early. AND THE COUSIN CLAIM IS NOW CERTAIN. Four acts agree: Anna Arlotta's death names her parents as Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa, who are Serafina Arlotta's parents; her husband's death names her back; Generosa's own death names that couple as her parents; and the 1888 marriage gave them first. ANNA AND SERAFINA WERE SISTERS, SO ROCCO AND GENEROSA WERE FIRST COUSINS. ANNA DIED ON 16 MARCH 1915 AND ANTONINO ON 1 JUNE, eleven weeks apart, in the same year her brother Domenico died two days after her.

source: Antenati name index — Sofi and Zirilli at Scilla
scope: cognome=Sofi (64 indexed persons, 20 of them the deceased) and cognome=Zirilli (10 indexed persons) at Scilla.
result: TWO NEGATIVES WORTH HAVING AND ONE STRUCTURAL FACT. NO ZIRILLI IS EVER THE DECEASED. All ten Zirilli in the index are mothers named inside somebody else's act, and GIOVANNA ZIRILLI -- Orazio Arena's wife -- appears FIVE TIMES that way: mother of Teresa Arena (d. 1913), Giuseppe Arena (d. 1922), Maria Annunziata Arena (d. 1933), Alessandro Antonio Arena (d. 1936) and a Mariantonia Costa (d. 1919). SHE DIED BEFORE 1911, which is the same reading as Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta. MARIA SOFI'S PARENTS ARE NOT HERE. Row 72 wants them; the index holds four women called Maria Sofi and NOT ONE is named as the wife of a Michele Donato. The one who died on 3 August 1913 carries no relations at all. The row stays open and stays a volume read. AND THE INDEX DOES NOT DEDUPLICATE PEOPLE -- this is the fact to carry forward. Each act generates its own person-record, so «Giovanna Zirilli» is five records and not one woman linked to five acts, and «69 Arena at Scilla» is sixty-nine MENTIONS across acts, not sixty-nine people. Anyone counting heads off this index will count wrong. NOTED IN PASSING: two Domenico Sofi, both «Padre Giorgio, Madre Maria Paladino», dying in 1933 and 1934 -- the same repeated-name pattern this archive reads as a child who died, except both of these reached adulthood, so it wants an act rather than an assumption. MARIA PALADINO is also the name in dispute at row 25, and this is a different family.

source: Antenati name index — Romano, Russo, Martello, Paladino and Pontillo at Scilla
scope: cognome=Romano (26 deceased), Russo (12), Martello, Paladino and Pontillo at Scilla. Martello and Paladino both hit the 100-row page cap and were not fully read.
result: THE ROMANO SWEEP FINISHED A LONG ARGUMENT. GIOVANNA ROMANO DIED AT SCILLA ON 15 JULY 1930 -- «Padre ANNUNZIATO, Madre ANGELA ZIRILLI, Coniuge CAMILLO ANTONIO POLISTENA». Her own act, her own surname, her own parents, her own husband. That is the FIFTH record calling her Romano and the first to give her parents, and it retires the tree's «Giuseppi Pontillo» and «Nunziatta Pontillo» for good. TWO MORE NEW ANCESTORS: ANNUNZIATO ROMANO and ANGELA ZIRILLI. AND A THREAD WORTH PULLING: Orazio Arena's wife was GIOVANNA ZIRILLI and Giovanna Romano's mother was ANGELA ZIRILLI -- two Zirilli women marrying into two of the four quarters, which in a town this size is more likely kinship than coincidence and is not yet evidence of it. NEGATIVE ON THE RUSSO: the only Concetta Russo in the index died on 20 May 1939 as the wife of a DOMENICO ROMANO, so she is not Giovanni Arena's wife. His own 1936 act names Concetta Russo as his spouse, so she either outlived the indexed span or died before 1911. PART, NOT DONE: Martello and Paladino returned the full hundred rows the page allows and will need paging or a given-name filter before either can be called searched.

source: Antenati name index — which of this family's comuni are indexed at all
scope: Queried the name index by locality alone for every comune this family touches: Scilla, Pizzo, Piedimonte Etneo, Briatico, Zambrone, San Costantino Calabro, Potenzoni and Catania — reading the act-type and year facets on each.
result: THE INDEX IS PATCHY BY COMUNE AND BY ACT TYPE, AND ASSUMING OTHERWISE WOULD HAVE COST A WEEK. INDEXED: SCILLA, deaths only, solid 1911-1943 with a scatter back to 1880. PIZZO, BIRTHS only, about 5,900 of them across 1868-1903 -- so «deaths only» was a SCILLA fact and not an Antenati one, and anyone generalising from one comune will guess wrong about the next. CATANIA, deaths, 34,294 from 1911. NOT INDEXED AT ALL, all returning «Nessun risultato trovato»: PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, BRIATICO, ZAMBRONE, SAN COSTANTINO CALABRO and POTENZONI. THAT IS THE WHOLE CALABRIAN SIDE EXCEPT PIZZO AND SCILLA, and the whole Sicilian side except Catania city. The Prostamo, the Melluso, the Anile and the Ventrice cannot be reached this way and stay volume reads. THE PORTAL SAYS SO ITSELF on a nil result: «solo una parte dei registri disponibili e stata completamente indicizzata». TWO NEGATIVES INSIDE THE INDEXED COMUNI: no PROSTAMO among Pizzo's indexed births, which is expected since the family was at Briatico by the 1868-1903 window; and no MAZZA or NICOTRA of this family at Catania. AND A CAUTION ABOUT THE PARAMETER ITSELF: «localita=» does NOT mean «the act was registered here». It matches ANY place attached to the person, birth or death, and apparently the historical province too -- localita=Catania returns people who died at VICOPISANO IN TUSCANY and at Catenanuova. It worked cleanly at Scilla only because the people there were born and died in the same town.

source: Antenati — Scilla, the pre-1866 death series listed
scope: The whole Stato civile della restaurazione death series for Scilla, listed in one page load via tipologia=Morti on serie 2002440 with s_size=100.
result: FIFTY-ONE VOLUMES, 1817 TO 1865, AND TWO ROWS THAT COULD NOT START NOW CAN. The archive held 55 Nati and 54 Matrimoni volumes for this period and NOT ONE Morti volume; the series had simply never been listed. NOTE THE START YEAR: the births begin in 1816 and the DEATHS BEGIN IN 1817, so either Scilla registered no deaths in its first year or that volume is gone. Anyone reasoning «civil registration begins in 1816» about a death is reasoning one year wrong. DOUBLED YEARS: 1846 and 1854 each have two volumes. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: FILIPPO ARENA and DOMENICA COSTA, both born in the 1790s and both alive when their son married in 1851, so dying most likely in the 1850s to 1870s -- the back half of this run and the front of the post-1866 one, and the only remaining route to a generation above Filippo. And DOMENICO ARLOTTA, the deepest name on the Scilla side, dead before April 1854 and therefore inside this run if he died after 1817. THE SERIES ID IS THE REUSABLE PART: serie 2002440 carries ALL THREE act types for the restaurazione period and is filtered by tipologia, exactly as 16594786 does for the italiano period.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1924, parte I, atto 83, read in full
scope: The death act of Camillo Antonio Polistena, found from the volume's own INDICE ANNUALE and read at 1800px. Container 5xGkdq3, image 45 of 75.
result: THE FIRST OF THE FOUR ACTS THE INDEX ONLY SUMMARISED, AND IT CORRECTS THE ARCHIVE BY NINE YEARS. «L'anno millenovecento ventiquattro addi diciannove di Ottobre, a ore otto e minuti quaranta ... e morto POLISTENA CAMILLO ANTONIO, di anni OTTANTA, PESCATORE, residente in questo Comune, nato in Scilla, dal fu GIUSEPPE, e dalla fu PONTILLO ANNA, MARITO DI ROMANO GIOVANNA.» AGED EIGHTY IN OCTOBER 1924 MEANS BORN ABOUT 1844. The archive carried «about 1835», which was inferred from his son's birth rather than read. HE DIED AT FIFTY MINUTES PAST MIDNIGHT at the house in RIONE MONACINA and the act was registered the same morning. THE DECLARANTS ARE BOTH FISHERMEN: Matra Camillo fu Giacomo, sixty-three, and POLISTENA ANTONIO FU LUIGI, twenty-eight -- a Polistena kinsman this archive does not hold. AND ONE WITNESS IS AN ARENA: «ARENA ROCCO FU FILIPPO, di anni trentasei, giornaliero». NOT THE ROCCO ARENA OF THIS FAMILY, who was sixty-three in 1924 and the son of Francesco Antonio -- this is the Rocco Arena son of Filippo and Clementina Furfari who died in 1938, and he is exactly the namesake row 132 warns about. THE METHOD IS THE REUSABLE PART: the volume's INDICE ANNUALE at image 74 gives «Polistena Camillo Antonio fu Giuseppe, parte 1a, numero 83», and the acts run TWO PER IMAGE, so act 83 is image 45. That is three downloads instead of seventy-five.

source: NAA — Mario Crupi's internment file and naturalisation record, read
scope: NameSearch for CRUPI Mario across all record categories: twelve items. The internee dossier NAA: MP1103/1, Q30124 is digitised and was read; the naturalisation record NAA: A714, 9/4300 carries its detail in the item title itself.
result: HE WAS NATURALISED IN APRIL 1940 AND INTERNED IN APRIL 1942 ANYWAY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. NAA A714 9/4300: «SURNAME CRUPI; GIVEN NAMES Mario; DATE OF NATURALISATION 26 APR 1940; PLACE OF BIRTH Piedimonte, Etneo Cattania, ITALY; PLACE OF RESIDENCE Ingham, QLD; ADDITIONAL INFORMATION Single.» He became a British subject two months before Italy entered the war. IT DID NOT PROTECT HIM. THE SERVICE AND CASUALTY FORM, A.A.F. A.112, identification Q.30124 -- the same number as his aliens registration certificate: «Date of Capture 20.4.42. Place of Capture BEMERSIDE, INGHAM. Date of Birth 28.11.05. Place of Birth Piedimonte, Prov. Catania, Italy. Trade or Occupation CANE CUTTER. Religion Roman Catholic. Nationality ITALIAN (NAT.). Marital Condition MARRIED. Next of Kin MARIA CRUPI, P.O. Bemerside Via Ingham, WIFE. Hair black, eyes brown.» HE WAS TAKEN AT HIS OWN ADDRESS. THE ROUTE IS ON THE SAME SHEET: interned at GAYTHORNE 26 April, marched in ex Gaythorne to COWRA on 5 May, transferred to LOVEDAY 13 August and marched in there 17 August 1942, sent to a TRIBUNAL in January 1943, and RELEASED 29 DECEMBER 1943 -- twenty months. AND IT PROVES SOMETHING THIS ARCHIVE REFUSED TO CLAIM. The 1959 electoral roll put a Mario and a Maria Crupi at Tully with the address column blank on both, and the refusal to pair them on adjacency alone was right; the next-of-kin line pairs them properly. IT ALSO DATES THE MARRIAGE to between 26 April 1940, when he was SINGLE, and 20 April 1942, when he was married. FIVE MORE FILES ARE NOT YET OPENED: BP242/1 Q25743, his Queensland investigation case file; A435 1946/4/2800; D1901 C594; MP1103/2 Q30124; and J25 1955/16646.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1932, parte I, atto 9, read in full
scope: Rocco Arena's death act, found from the volume's INDICE ANNUALE («Arena Rocco fu Francesco Antonio, parte Ia, numero 9») and read at 1800px. Container w6zPMA1, image 8 of 63.
result: THE SECOND OF THE FOUR ACTS, AND IT CLOSES THE AMERICAN STORY IN THE PLACE IT STARTED. «e morto ARENA ROCCO, di anni SETTANTUNO, PESCATORE, residente in Scilla, nato in questo Comune, dal fu FRANCESCO ANTONIO e dalla fu ARLOTTA SERAFINA, VEDOVO DI COSTA GENEROSA.» HE DIED AT A QUARTER PAST SIX IN THE EVENING ON 8 FEBRUARY 1932, at the house in VIA PROF. ZAGARI, and the act was drawn the following morning. A FISHERMAN AND A WIDOWER. Generosa Costa had died in June 1916 and he outlived her by fifteen years and eight months. EVERY NAME AGREES WITH THE ARCHIVE: both parents, the wife, the town. WHAT IS NEW IS THE ADDRESS, THE TRADE AND THE HOUR. ONE SMALL TENSION, RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: «di anni settantuno» would put his birth before February 1861, but his birth act is Nati 1861 ATTO 228, late in the year, and the 1900 US census says September 1861 -- which makes him SEVENTY. The birth act wins; an age on a death act is what two elderly neighbours told the registrar. THE COMPANY HE DIED AMONG IS WORTH NOTING: the declarants and witnesses are PONTILLO ROCCO FU GIOVANNI, LAMERI GIUSEPPE FU LUIGI, PONTILLO SANTO FU GIOVANNI and ALFONZETTI ROCCO FU ANTONINO -- two Pontillo brothers among them, in a street of fishermen, all four signing with a mark.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1936, parte I, atti 14 and 20, read in full
scope: The death acts of Giovanni Arena and Michele Donato, both in the 1936 volume, found from its INDICE ANNUALE and read. Container 0AVjBab, images 10 and 13 of 57.
result: THE LAST TWO OF THE FOUR ACTS, AND THEY PUT TWO QUARTERS OF THIS FAMILY ON THE SAME STREET. GIOVANNI ARENA, atto 14: died 31 MARCH 1936 at nine in the morning, VIA GROTTE 72, «di anni OTTANTUNO, MARINAIO, dal fu ANTONIO e dalla fu ARLOTTA SERAFINA, MARITO DI RUSSO CONCETTA». The age is exact -- born 30 April 1854, he was eighty-one and a month short of eighty-two. His wife was still living. MICHELE DONATO, atto 20: died 10 MAY 1936 at six in the morning, VIA GROTTE 66, «di anni OTTANTA, MARINAIO, dal fu DOMENICO e da fu SOFI NUNZIATA, MARITO DI SOFI MARIA». SIXTY YARDS AND SIX WEEKS APART. AND ONE CORRECTION: the tree has Michele Donato born in 1851, which would make him eighty-five here and fifty-seven on the New Orleans manifest of 1908 that calls him fifty-two. THE DEATH ACT AND THE MANIFEST BOTH POINT AT 1855 OR 1856 and the tree is five years out. THE STREET IS THE LARGER FINDING AND IT WAS ALREADY IN THE ARCHIVE UNNOTICED: Fortunato Arena born at VIA GROTTE 70 in 1891, Giuseppe Arena at 75 in 1892, Maria Donato at 21 in 1888, Giovanni Polistena at 47 in 1883. THREE OF THE FOUR SCILLA QUARTERS LIVED ON ONE STREET, which is how they kept marrying each other. BOTH ACTS ALSO SHARE THEIR WITNESSES -- Mulinaro Domenico, twenty-two, a driver, and Delorenzo Rocco, thirty-three, an attendant -- who are municipal regulars rather than family.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1912, parte I, atto 83, read in full
scope: The act behind the index line this archive read as Serafina Arena's death. Found from the volume's own INDICE — «Arena Serafina, di Rocco, Agosto 15, Numero 83, Parte 1a, Pagina 22» — and read. Container LeplDll, image 45 of 93.
result: IT IS NOT THE SERAFINA THIS ARCHIVE THOUGHT, AND THE ROW BUILT ON IT IS RETRACTED. «e morta ARENA SERAFINA, DI MESI TRE, residente in Scilla, NATA IN QUESTO COMUNE, da ROCCO, marinaro, domiciliato in Scilla, e da GENEROSA COSTA, casalinga.» THREE MONTHS OLD AND BORN AT SCILLA. Yesterday this archive recorded that Serafina Arena, baptised at Our Lady of Loretto in Manhattan on 15 August 1898, had died at Scilla on her FOURTEENTH BIRTHDAY. The matching dates were what made it persuasive and they were a coincidence. WHAT MISLED ME IS WORTH NAMING: Antenati's name index prints «Nascita: Scilla» on these entries and I decided that field was a default rather than a claim, because believing it was inconvenient. IT WAS A CLAIM AND IT WAS CORRECT. WHAT IS FOUND INSTEAD IS A CHILD NOBODY HERE KNEW OF: Rocco Arena and Generosa Costa had a SECOND SERAFINA, born at Scilla about May 1912 in the QUARTIERE CHIANALEA, dead at three months. THEY GAVE THE NAME AGAIN FOURTEEN YEARS AFTER THE FIRST, which is the same reading this archive makes of their two sons named Antonio. AND IT PROVES SOMETHING ABOUT THE HOUSEHOLD: they were at Scilla and still having children in 1912, which is the return from America seen from the inside rather than inferred from three absences. GENEROSA COSTA WAS ABOUT FORTY-FOUR. THE NEW YORK SERAFINA HAS NO KNOWN FATE AGAIN. The act also gives Rocco as MARINARO, where his own death act of 1932 calls him PESCATORE.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1915, parte I, atti 34 and 36, read in full
scope: The death acts of Domenico and Anna Arlotta, two days apart in March 1915, found from the volume's own INDICE and read. Container Lq2qDbM, images 20 and 21 of 95.
result: THE ACTS CONFIRM THE PARENTS AND DEFLATE MY OWN FRAMING OF THE DATES. DOMENICO ARLOTTA, atto 34: died at noon on 14 MARCH 1915 at the RIONE CHIANALEA, «di anni SETTANTATRE, MARINARO ... da fu GIOVANNI e da fu COSTA MARIA, marito di PONTILLO MARIA». ANNA ARLOTTA, atto 36: died at four in the morning on 16 MARCH 1915 at the QUARTIERE CHIANALEA, «di anni OTTANTA, casalinga ... da fu GIOVANNI e da fu COSTA MARIA, MOGLIE DI COSTA ANTONINO». BOTH PARENTS NAMED ON BOTH ACTS, so the sibling link and the cousin chain behind it now rest on the ACTS and not on an index line. Their ages date them: Anna about 1835, Domenico about 1842, against Serafina Arlotta's documented 13 June 1830. THE ROW ASKED WHETHER AN EPIDEMIC OR THE SEA TOOK THEM. NEITHER ACT SAYS, BECAUSE ITALIAN CIVIL DEATH ACTS DO NOT RECORD A CAUSE. AND THE ARITHMETIC TAKES THE DRAMA OUT OF IT: Scilla registered about a hundred and twenty-five deaths in 1915, which is one every three days, so TWO DEATHS IN A WEEK IS THE ORDINARY RATE and a third, ARENA FILIPPO on 17 March, makes three in four days without meaning anything either. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NOTABLE IS NOT THE TIMING BUT THE ADDRESS: both died in CHIANALEA, the fishing quarter -- where ROCCO ARENA AND GENEROSA COSTA'S INFANT DAUGHTER had died three years earlier. An eighty-year-old and her brother of seventy-three, in the same quarter, two days apart, is most simply one household and one illness; the register will not say so and this archive should not either.

source: Antenati — Scilla, the annual death indexes of 1897–1908
scope: The A section of every annual death index from 1897 to 1908 — twelve years, less 1909, which Antenati does not hold — read at full resolution for FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA and SERAFINA ARLOTTA. Containers for all twelve are saved in scilla-arks-italiano.tsv.
result: BOTH FOUND, AND THE SWEEP IS FINISHED. FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA died 29 AUGUST 1901 — Morti 1901, parte I, atto 96 — and SERAFINA ARLOTTA died 24 APRIL 1908 — Morti 1908, parte I, atto 55 — BOTH AT VIA GROTTE NUMBER TWO, the same house, six years and eight months apart. Read in full in scilla-reads. THE YEARS THAT WERE CLEAR, kept so no one reads them again. 1897: Arena Nicolina di Filippo (10), two Anastasi, Arbitrio Antonio (111), Arlotta Antonio di Rocco (144), Arlotta Giuseppa di Filippo (185), Andaloro Pasquale (200). 1898: Alfonzetti Concetta (4), Arbitrio Rocco (44), Arena Rocco di Rocco (55), Anastasi Antonio (88), an ARENA FRANCESCO GIOVANNI with no act number written, Arena Rocco di Giuseppe (91), Alfonzetti Maria (102), Alfonzetti Antonia (109). 1899: five entries and no Arena at all. 1900: clear. 1902: ONE ENTRY IN THE WHOLE YEAR — Andaloro Maria Antonia fu Francesco (76) — and not a single Arena or Arlotta death in a town where both are among the commonest names. 1903: Alfonzetti Michelangelo fu Onofrio, Arlotta Rocco fu Orazio, Arlotta Maria di Filippo. 1905: Arlotta Maria fu Antonio (1), Arlotta Rosaria fu Pasquale (12), Arbitrio Giuseppe di Natale (28), Arena Rocco fu Orazio (70), Alfonzetti Giuseppe (113), Andaloro Anna Maria (138). 1907: TWO ENTRIES — Arlotta Antonio fu Orazio (20) and Arbitrio Marianna di Rocco (124).
