SIX LEADS LEFT LYING, all Arena, none yet read: Arena Raffaele fu Giuseppe (1901, atto 63); ARENA COSMO DI FILIPPO (1904, atto 122) — a LIVING father Filippo, and Rocco Arena's eldest brother Filippo, born 1852, would be fifty-two that year; ARENA NICOLINA DI GIUSEPPE (1906, atto 41) — Rocco's brother Giuseppe, born 1860, married Maria Martello in 1885; Arena Rocco di Alessandro (1906, atto 141); ARENA GIOVANNA DI ROCCO (1908, parte II, atto 2); and Arena Santo fu Rocco (1908, atto 108). THE METHOD, WHICH IS THE PART THAT TRANSFERS. Container ids cost one rate-limited page load each and are SAVED; manifests and images fetch to curl unlimited. The index sits at a different offset in every volume — n−6 to n−9 across these twelve — so tools/antenati_index.py montages the last six to ten images into one contact sheet, read once to locate the A page. THE SCAN OFTEN CROPS THE LEFT PAGE'S SURNAME COLUMN, and the frame BEFORE it re-shoots the same opening whole: that alone rescued 1904 and 1908. Acts run FOUR to an opening, so act-to-image is arithmetic off any one calibration. AND SEE THE CORRECTION FILED WITH THIS ROW: the 1908 index entered Serafina Arlotta under her HUSBAND'S surname, Arena.

source: The National Archives (UK), Discovery — every surname and town of this family
scope: Discovery's public JSON API, https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/API/search/records?sps.searchQuery=..., queried for PROSTAMO, POLISTENA, CRUPI, ARLOTTA, VENTRICE, MELLUSO, CICHELLO, ZIRILLI, FRAGALA, and for the towns SCILLA, BRIATICO and PIEDIMONTE ETNEO.
result: NOTHING HERE FOR THIS FAMILY, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN BAD LUCK. ZERO RESULTS for PROSTAMO, POLISTENA, CICHELLO, ZIRILLI, FRAGALA, BRIATICO and PIEDIMONTE ETNEO. The few hits on the other names are demonstrably other people: CRUPI returns a Royal Warwickshire medal card for a «Crupie, C A» and a photograph of Monreale cathedral; ARLOTTA returns a merchant seaman born at UDINE in 1934 and a naturalisation for a Maria Arlotta Cook born 1923; MELLUSO returns an academic paper. WHY IT WAS ALWAYS UNLIKELY: this family moved ITALY TO AUSTRALIA and ITALY TO NEW YORK and never through Britain. The Kew series that would matter -- BT 26 and BT 27, the inward and outward passenger lists -- cover UK PORTS ONLY, and every crossing this archive holds left Genoa, Messina or Naples. ONE ANGLE IS NOT CLOSED AND IS WORTH A ROW: TNA holds MERCHANT SEAMEN records that DO carry an Italian birthplace -- BT 372 registry cards and BT 99 crew agreements, the latter showing entries like «place of birth, Napoli» -- and this family is full of MARINAI: Giovanni Arena and Michele Donato are both «marinaio» on their 1936 acts, Domenico Arlotta on his of 1915, Antonino Prostamo «marinaro». If any of them ever signed on a BRITISH-REGISTERED ship they would be in these series. It is a long shot and it is a real one. AND A TRAP WORTH THE RECORD: Discovery throttles with HTTP 202 AND AN EMPTY BODY. A scraper reads that as zero results, which is exactly how a rate limit becomes a published negative -- the same failure shape as Antenati's 403 and Findmypast's dead parameters. Poll until 200 and a non-empty body before believing any count.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1908 parte II, the transcribed foreign deaths
scope: Parte II of the 1908 Scilla death volume, opened to chase «Arena Giovanna di Rocco» from the annual index — a possible daughter of Rocco Arena.
result: THE LEAD CLOSES AND A WHOLE SERIES OPENS. Arena Giovanna, nine, born at Scilla, died AT MARSEILLE on 1 February 1905; her mother is FRANCESCA MARTELLO, not Generosa Costa, so she is not Rocco Arena's daughter. But PARTE II OF A SCILLA DEATH VOLUME IS A REGISTER OF DEATHS ABROAD, transcribed on the order of the Procuratore del Re at Reggio from certificates issued by foreign authorities, and this archive has never opened one. The 1908 parte II holds five acts and three of them are foreign: NEW YORK (Gulli Rocco, 27, a fractured skull, 17 August 1907, transcribed from an English certificate with a translation at his widow's request), MARSEILLE and TUNIS. Rocco Arena crossed to New York four times and Giovanni Arena followed him in 1899. Parte II sits at the back of each volume immediately before the annual index and is only a few acts long, so eighty-one volumes is an affordable sweep, not a dream.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Morti 1904 atto 122 and 1906 atto 41, the two best Arena leads
scope: The two leads out of the 1897–1908 index sweep that named a LIVING father whose name this archive already holds: «Arena Cosmo di Filippo» (1904) and «Arena Nicolina di Giuseppe» (1906). Rocco Arena's brothers are a Filippo born 1852 and a Giuseppe born 1860.
result: ONE CLEAN NEGATIVE AND ONE CANDIDATE THAT NEEDS A MARRIAGE ACT. ARENA NICOLINA IS NOT GIUSEPPE ARENA'S DAUGHTER. She was FORTY when she died on 14 March 1906 at Via Grotte 17 — born about 1866, when Rocco's brother Giuseppe was six. Her father is another Giuseppe Arena, pescatore, still living; her mother the late MARIANNA ROMANO; her husband Giuseppe Cesoriero. That makes a FOURTH distinct Arena household at Scilla. ARENA COSMO IS CLOSED TOO, AN HOUR LATER AND FOR NOTHING.  Three months old, dead 1 December 1904 at VICO SAN MICHELE 13, son of FILIPPO, pescatore, and CLEMENTINA FARFARI, lavandaia. THE ACT GIVES THE FATHER NO AGE, so whether this Filippo is Rocco's eldest brother, born 14 February 1852, cannot be settled here. THE TEST IS FILIPPO ARENA'S MARRIAGE ACT, which names his parents; Scilla's civil marriages 1866–1913 are all on Antenati and a man born 1852 married about 1875–1885. A SIDEWAYS PROOF WORTH HAVING: CESORIERO DOMENICO, becchino, is 46 in August 1901 declaring Francesco Antonio Arena's death and 49 in December 1904 declaring this child's — three years and four months, exact. Two gravediggers buried this parish for a decade and their ages hold. RESOLVED BY ONE QUERY INSTEAD OF TEN VOLUMES. The plan was to sweep Scilla's annual MARRIAGE indexes 1874-1885 for Filippo Arena's wedding; seven of those years had no container saved and would have cost a rate-limited page load each before a single image. Instead the ANTENATI NAME INDEX, which carries the SPOUSE, was re-read: FILIPPO ARENA died at Scilla on 17 MARCH 1915, «Padre GIOVANNI ARENA, Madre NATALINA LONGORDO, Coniuge CLEMENTINA FURFARI», and a son of his, ROCCO ARENA, died 31 March 1938 with the same parents. So Cosmo's father is the son of Giovanni Arena and Natalina Longordo, NOT of Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta. ARENA COSMO IS NOT ROCCO ARENA'S NEPHEW, and Rocco's brother Filippo is still missing. THE INDEX ALSO CORRECTED MY TRANSCRIPTION: FURFARI, not Farfari. THE LESSON IS THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS. When a question is «who were this man's parents», ask the NAME INDEX before planning a volume sweep -- it answers with father, mother and spouse in one GET, and it covers 1910-1943, which reaches back over anyone who was alive then.

source: Antenati name index — the six Scilla surnames re-run and WRITTEN OUT IN FULL
scope: Arlotta, Costa, Donato, Polistena, Romano, Pontillo and Musolino at Scilla, «cerca per nome», s_size=100, paced at 4–4.5 seconds and control-tested against «403 Forbidden» on every fetch. All seven had been run before by earlier sessions (rows 128, 130, 131, 132); this pass existed to WRITE THE DECEASED OUT IN FULL rather than summarise them.
result: THE COUNTS. Arlotta 75 records / 24 deceased. Costa 76 / 18. Donato 26 / 11. Polistena 73 / 25. Romano 79 / 26. Pontillo 50 / 24. MUSOLINO 7 / 2. THE NEGATIVE THAT ANSWERS A ROW. MARIANTONIA MUSOLINO — Orazio Arena's apparent second wife — IS NOT IN THE INDEX. Scilla has only seven Musolino records at all and the two deceased are Domenico Musolino (d. 17 April 1911, son of Bruno Musolino and Grazia Longordo) and Francesca Musolino (d. 7 November 1928, father Francesco). Neither is she. She is named only from inside her son's act. So she died outside 1911–1943 or away from Scilla, and the ONLY remaining route to her is Orazio Arena's second marriage act. FOUR HOUSEHOLDS WRITTEN INTO corrections.tsv: Giovanna Romano's three sisters (Maria d. 1917 m. Giovanni Cardona, Concetta d. 1926 m. ROCCO DONATO, Mariantonia d. 1930 m. Matteo Bova); the four children of Lorenzo Costa and Generosa Polistena, including GENEROSA COSTA'S OWN FATHER Antonio, d. 1 June 1915; Domenico Arlotta's wife MARIA PONTILLO, d. 1922, with her parents; and the guard on the two Generosa Costas. FOUR DONATO–POLISTENA TIES, NOT TWO, which is what row 138 wants: Maria Donato d. 1911, wife of GIUSEPPE POLISTINA; Raffaele Polistena x TERESA DONATO, whose children Santa (1926), Maria (1927) and Luigi (1933) all die at Scilla; Giovanni Polistena x ANNUNZIATA DONATO, whose daughter Teresa dies in 1933; and Rocco Polistena, d. 1923, husband of NUNZIATA POLISTENA — a Polistena marrying a Polistena, which is the surname endogamy this archive has already met among the Bueti and the Vizzari. AND THE HONEST COST OF THIS PASS. Every one of these seven surnames had already been queried, days ago, and the results summarised in a sentence apiece. Because they were summarised, they had to be fetched again. THE RULE, NOW STATED TWICE IN ONE DAY: when a query returns a bounded set — twenty-six rows, not twenty-six thousand — WRITE THE SET DOWN. The cost of the paragraph is smaller than the cost of the second search, and the second search is rate-limited.

source: Antenati — the complete Scilla register list, all three fondi
scope: /search-registry/?localita=Scilla&s_size=500 — every register Antenati holds for the comune, in one page load, to find out whether the marriage PROCESSETTI exist for the Arena weddings of 1885 and 1888.
result: 466 REGISTERS. 17 napoleonic, 182 restaurazione, 267 italiano. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED IS NO: there are TWENTY-TWO processetti volumes and they run 1810 to 1865 and STOP. The Italian-era fondo holds none, so the 1885 and 1888 bundles are not on Antenati and row 64's Italian half is closed. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION NOT ASKED IS MUCH BETTER. Francesco Antonio Arena and Serafina Arlotta married 7 FEBRUARY 1851, and the bundle for it is the volume 1849-1852, ark an_ua2002487. Processetti carry both spouses' BIRTH extracts and the DEATH acts of dead parents -- and the Scilla bundle of 1842-1845 carried a dead grandparent as well. One volume therefore attacks row 68 (Filippo Arena and Domenica Costa's deaths), row 39 (Giovanni Arlotta x Maria Costa's marriage) and row 85 (Domenico Arlotta) at once. AND SCILLA'S REGISTRATION BEGINS IN 1809, NOT 1816. This archive has been saying 1816 and planning around it -- see the caution written after Domenico Arlotta. Seven unopened years: Matrimoni and Morti 1809; Matrimoni, Morti and Nati 1810, 1811, 1812 and 1815; Matrimoni 1813-1814. All arks now in data/scilla-arks.tsv. PARAMETER TRAP, RECORDED: ?citta=Scilla returns ZERO with no error; ?localita=Scilla returns 466. Control-test before believing a nil.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni processetti 1849–1852, fascicolo 13 of 1851, read in full
scope: The marriage bundle of FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA and SERAFINA ARLOTTA, 7 February 1851 — found by listing Scilla's registers, buying one container, and locating the fascicolo wrapper by SHAPE in a thumbnail montage.
result: FOUR SHEETS, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE WORTH THE WHOLE DAY. FOGLIO 1 — FRANCESCO ANTONIO ARENA'S BIRTH ACT, act 186 of 1819, the ACT and not the Tavola this archive has been citing. 25 November 1819, twelve o'clock, in the family's own house. FILIPPO ARENA, DI ANNI VENTICINQUE, MARINARO -- born about 1794 -- and DOMENICA COSTA, DI ANNI VENTISETTE -- born about 1792. Two generation-seven people who had no dates at all now have ages, from an act in which Filippo appeared in person. AND HE SIGNED IT, in a register where almost every act ends «perche illetterati». Baptised the next day at the Parrocchia di Scilla. FOGLIO 2 — SERAFINA ARLOTTA'S BIRTH ACT, AND IT IS ACT 89, NOT ACT 2. This archive cites «Nati 1830 atto 2» in three places; 2 is a Tavola row number. The date holds: born 13 JUNE 1830 AT TWO IN THE NIGHT in her parents' house, declared next afternoon by her father. MARIA COSTA, DI ANNI VENTITRE -- born about 1807, her first date of any kind. And GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, DI ANNI QUARANTA -- born about 1790, which CONFLICTS BY ELEVEN YEARS with his own 1854 declaration of seventy-five. Flagged, not averaged. Witness DOMENICO COSTA, commerciante, 46, produced by the father: a candidate for Maria Costa's own father and nothing more. WHAT THE BUNDLE DOES NOT CONTAIN IS ALSO EVIDENCE. No death act of any parent, where fascicolo 3 of the same year binds in «Atto di morte del padre e dell'avo paterno dello Sposo». The ordinary reading is that all four parents were alive on 7 February 1851. Graded inferred, because the bride was twenty and no consent sheet is listed either. NAVIGATION, WHICH IS THE REUSABLE PART. The volume is 1845 images over four years and its interior order is loose. Each fascicolo opens with a WRAPPER — nearly blank left page, short centred list on the right — and wrappers are findable BY SHAPE in a montage of thumbnails at width 430, with no text read at all. In 1851 they sit at images 1100 (num. 3), 1190 (num. 13), 1280 (num. 24), 1430 (num. 37). DO NOT navigate by the «Num. d'ordine» on the atti di notificazione bound inside: that is a separate publication series running at a different rate, and following it walks you into the wrong month.

source: Antenati — Giovanni Arlotta x Maria Costa's marriage: three processetti volumes sized, then rate-limited
scope: The marriage that would settle Giovanni Arlotta's eleven-year age conflict and decide whether the Domenico Arlotta generation belongs to this family. Serafina Arlotta was born 13 June 1830, so the wedding is 1829 or earlier; the candidate bundles are Scilla processetti 1828-1831 and 1824-1827.
result: NOT FOUND YET, AND THE GROUND IS PREPARED. CONTAINERS BOUGHT AND SAVED: 1828-1831 = LD6PQKn (1296 images), 1824-1827 = 5xYoOBO (1416 images), and 1849-1852 = 58rXBoX (1845 images). YEAR MAP FOR LD6PQKn, read off a ten-point thumbnail scan: 1830 runs roughly images 700-1000 -- wrappers dated «Anno 1830» sit at images 740 and 880 -- which puts 1829 at roughly 450-700 and 1828 before that. THE VOLUME HAS NO YEAR INDEX: its last six images are ordinary documents, not a tavola, so the fascicolo wrappers are the only finding aid. THEN THE RATE LIMITER. Three ark lookups for the Scilla MARRIAGE registers of 1828, 1829 and 1830 -- the cheaper route, because an annual marriage Tavola gives the act number and the fascicolo number follows it -- ALL THREE RETURNED «403 Forbidden». Caught by the control test and recorded as a block, NOT as three absent registers. That distinction is the whole reason the test exists. The arks are in scilla-arks.tsv (1828 an_ua2002545, 1829 an_ua2002548, 1830 an_ua2002551); only the containers are owed, and they cost one paced page load each once the block lifts. IMAGES ARE NOT RATE LIMITED and never were -- the whole thumbnail scan above was run while the HTML side was blocked.

source: NAA — Antonino Crupi's aliens registration card, read in full; and the whole CRUPI name index
scope: NameSearch on CRUPI across ALL record categories — 233 items, pulled 200 to a page and read end to end — then the D4028 card for Antonino Crupi, both sides, at full resolution.
result: THE CARD. NAA: D4028, CRUPI ANTONIO, item 9209610, digitised and free. Certificate Q 5949 / Q 7838. ANTONINO CRUPI, born 5 OCTOBER 1907 at PIEDIMONTE ETNEO, ITALY. A BOOT REPAIRER. Address Box 484, Ingham; Abbott Street, Ingham. MARRIED. Entered Australia 2 SEPTEMBER 1930, PORT OF DEBARKATION BRISBANE. Five feet four; eyes black; hair black; build sturdy; NOTABLE MARKS: THE FOURTH FINGER OF THE RIGHT HAND DEFORMED. Registered 3 OCTOBER 1939 at INGHAM police station. HE WAS INTERNED, AND THAT IS THE THIRD MAN. The front is stamped LOVEDAY 35924. The CHANGE OF ADDRESS panel on the reverse reads «ex Gay[thorne] to 14A 16.3.43», then «LCCE 1/207 2.4.43 MAIL EXTRACT to wife, Q'land», then «22/10/43 Released and returned to Queensland». So: moved into Loveday compound 14A in March 1943 and released seven months later. ROSARIO MAZZA was interned on his own dossier; MARIO CRUPI at Loveday from 18 August 1942 to 30 December 1943; ANTONINO CRUPI released 22 October 1943. Angela Crupi's husband and two of her brothers, all three behind wire in the same eighteen months. AND THE CENSOR COPIED A SENTENCE OF HIS ONTO HIS REGISTRATION CARD. The mail extract of 2 April 1943, from a letter to his wife in Queensland, is quoted on the card: «... Our freedom will come soon and we shall always cry Vive Italia.» It is the only sentence of his own that this archive has, and it survives because an official wrote it down as evidence against him. Read across two overlapping enlargements; the middle words are the least certain. PIETRO HAS NO CARD, AND THE REASON IS A FINDING. NAA: BP4/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P: «Alien Registration Certificate NOT ISSUED», the folio noting he was NATURALISED 23 FEBRUARY 1932. By 1939 he was a British subject and outside the series entirely. THE TWO BROTHERS CAME TOGETHER. NAA: BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI P and CRUPI A both read «arrived in Brisbane on OTRANTO 19 AUGUST 1930» -- Pietro born 1898, Antonino born 1907. Antonino's own card gives his entry as 2 September, two weeks after the ship docked: the same two-true-dates pattern already recorded for the passenger index. And BP9/3 ITALIAN CRUPI M names MARIO'S ship: «Crupi, Mariano born 1905 -- arrived in Brisbane on MARIA CRISTINA 20 MAY 1928», against the 13 June 1928 on his card. TWO NATURALISATIONS. A714 57/18792: ANTONINO naturalised 7 NOVEMBER 1946, born 1907 at Piedimonte, RESIDENT AT TULLY, wife NELLIE. A714 9/4300: MARIO naturalised 26 APRIL 1940, born 1905, resident at Ingham, SINGLE. THE TRAP, AND IT IS ONE BARCODE AWAY. Item 9209609 is ALSO a D4028 card for a CRUPI ANTONIO -- born at SERRATA, arrived MELBOURNE 20 October 1926. Serrata is in Calabria, not Sicily. Three consecutive barcodes, 9209609 / 9209610 / 9209611, and the middle and last are this family while the first is a stranger with the same name. Adjacency in an alphabetical card series is not kinship. ONE CONFLICT LEFT OPEN. The card says MARRIED in October 1939, and this archive notes an Antonino Crupi marrying in Queensland on 24 AUGUST 1940. Either that marriage is another man, or «married» was written on the card later. Not resolved here. UNREAD AND WANTED: NAA: BP242/1 Q16634, «Crupi, Antonio and Maria -- Queensland investigation case file», 1939-1957, Brisbane, ACCESS OPEN. That is very likely Antonino's own security file and it is the document behind the internment.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete PROSTAMO set, all thirteen items, and POSTAMO as a control
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on PROSTAMO — chasing Domenica Prostamo's March 1951 crossing (row 21) and testing whether she is hidden under the POSTAMO spelling that the Queensland death index uses for her.
result: POSTAMO RETURNS ZERO AND IT IS A TRUE NIL. «No records match the search criteria» — and the control, PROSTAMO, returns thirteen on the same form in the same minute. Queensland's registrar writes her POSTAMO on her daughter's death registration; the National Archives does not. DOMENICA PROSTAMO'S 1951 CROSSING IS STILL NOT THERE. She appears only inside her husband's file title, J25 1971/1074, «Mazza, Sebastiano; wife Domenica [nee Prostamo]». ALL THIRTEEN, WRITTEN OUT. B78 ITALIAN/PROSTAMO ROCCO: Rocco Prostamo, arrived MELBOURNE per NAPOLI 15 August 1949 (6423720). BP25/1 ITALIAN PROSTAMO F: Francesco Prostamo, arrived BRISBANE on the T/v ROMA 21 OCTOBER 1957 (5067016). BP25/1 ITALIAN TRUNGADI F: «Trungadi [nee Prostamo], Francesca», arrived BRISBANE on the T/v ROMA 21 OCTOBER 1957 (5080545). B78 ITALIAN/PROSTAMO FRANCESCA: a DIFFERENT Francesca, arrived MELBOURNE per OCEANIA 5 January 1956, «also known as CORSO» (6423719). PP14/3 ITALIAN/PROSTAMO G: GABRIELE PROSTAMO, Perth, application for registration as alien, CIRCA 1916-1920 (5137304). PP14/3 ITALIAN/PROSTAMO F: FRANCESCO PROSTAMO, Perth, same series, CIRCA 1916-1920 (5137303). J25 1971/1074: Mazza, Sebastiano; wife Domenica [nee Prostamo] (5121679). J25 1962/5930: Prostamo, Domenico Francesco; wife ASSUNTE MARIA [nee MELLUSO] (1682238). J25 1972/23086: Melluso, Gregorio; wife Carmela; and children Giuseppe, Maria [surname PROSTAMO] (5072628). J25 1961/3716: PROSTAMO, Antonino Giacomo and Angela [nee TOMSIC] (12901469). J25 1963/2810: Prostamo, Francesco (1681780). B44 V1974/35793: Prostamo, Francesca, Melbourne (4011946). B44 V1970/39910: Prostamo, R, Melbourne (14758061). THE CORRECTION THIS SET FORCES. This archive has Francesco Prostamo arriving at FREMANTLE on 10 OCTOBER 1957, graded «documented» because the NAA passenger index, the ship and the embarkation port all agreed. THE BRISBANE ALIENS SERIES SAYS HE ARRIVED AT BRISBANE ON 21 OCTOBER. Both are true and they answer different questions: 10 October is when the ROMA first touched Australia, 21 October is when he got off it. The family settled in Queensland, and the port of debarkation is the one that says so. Same for Francesca, on the same voyage. A NAME TO WATCH, NOT TO MERGE. The catalogue calls her «TRUNGADI [nee Prostamo], Francesca». The manifest, read in the original, makes the Francesca on that voyage FRANCESCO'S DAUGHTER, BORN 1945 AT BRIATICO, AGED TWELVE -- and a twelve-year-old is not «nee» anything. The likeliest reading is that the registration card was annotated with a married name years later and the catalogue transcribed the card's final state. TRUNGADI is therefore a married surname to look for, not a second woman. AND TWO PROSTAMO IN WESTERN AUSTRALIA IN THE FIRST WORLD WAR. PP14/3 holds alien registration applications for GABRIELE PROSTAMO and FRANCESCO PROSTAMO at Perth, CIRCA 1916-1920 -- thirty years earlier than anything this archive holds in Australia, and in the wrong state. Unread.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete POLISTENA set, fifty items, separated from the town of the same name
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on POLISTENA, read out in full at 200 to a page.
result: FIFTY ITEMS, AND THE FIRST THING TO DO WITH THEM IS SPLIT THEM IN TWO. POLISTENA IS A COMUNE IN REGGIO CALABRIA AS WELL AS A SURNAME, and NameSearch does not know the difference: four A714 naturalisations come back for men named OLIMPIO, MARFEA, FOGLIADORO and PALESTRI whose PLACE OF BIRTH is Polistena, and three A7919 prisoner-of-war records for SAVARESE, ROSSI and BOTTIGLIERI, born there and captured in Africa. THIS ARCHIVE'S POLISTENA ARE FROM SCILLA, seventy kilometres away. Seven of the fifty are the town, not the family. THREE HITS THAT MATTER. ONE. J25 1971/3900, Brisbane, 1953-1971: «ARENA, ROCCO; WIFE ANGELINA [OR ANGELA] [NEE POLISTENA]». Row 80 of the work list says their marriage «is not documented anywhere in this archive». HERE IS A COMMONWEALTH FILE THAT NAMES THEM AS HUSBAND AND WIFE AND GIVES HER MAIDEN NAME. It does not date the marriage; it proves it and it names the file that may. Not yet examined, held at Brisbane. TWO. BP9/3, ITALIAN POLISTENA G: «Polistena, GIOVANNI BORN 1883 - arrived in BRISBANE on the ORMONDE on 21 FEBRUARY 1928». This archive's GIOVANNI POLISTENA was born at Scilla in 1883, act 206, and is already documented sailing from PALERMO to NEW ORLEANS on the LIGURIA in February 1908, on the line immediately after Michele Donato. A SECOND MIGRATION, TWENTY YEARS LATER AND TO THE OTHER SIDE OF THE WORLD, would explain how this family reached Queensland at all. The year of birth matches exactly and the port is the right one. IT IS A CANDIDATE AND NOT A FINDING: the entry carries no parents and no birthplace. The test is the item itself, or a Queensland record placing him there in the 1930s. THREE. TWO MORE DONATO-POLISTENA MARRIAGES, IN QUEENSLAND THIS TIME. J25 1967/9873: «Polistena, Giuseppe; wife MARIA MADDALENA [NEE DONATO]». J25 1970/3023: «DONATO, CONCETTA [NEE POLISTENA]». With the four already found in the Scilla death index, that is SIX marriages between these two families across two countries and two generations. THE REST OF THE FAMILY-PLAUSIBLE ITEMS, written out so nobody pays for this again. SP908/1 (Sydney aliens): Maria Angela Polistena [nee Lipari], NEPTUNIA 24 May 1954; Annunziata Lipari also known as Polistena, ROMA 26 Nov 1964; Domenico Polistena, SURRIENTO 20 July 1950; Vincenzo Polistena, SURRIENTO 20 July 1950; Maria Carmela Polistena [nee Multari], aircraft 31 Aug 1963; Annunziato, Salvatore and Antonino Polistena, all aircraft 31 Aug 1963; Bellardina Polistena, SYDNEY 22 June 1957; Maria Vincenza Polistena, ROMA 26 Nov 1964. BP289/1 (Brisbane): Giuseppe, Fremantle 21 Mar 1968; Maria Pace, Sydney 29 June 1968; Maria, Brisbane 9 May 1964; Teresa, Brisbane 6 Mar 1965. B78 (Melbourne): Carmelo, 7 June 1964; Vincenzo, UGOLINO VIVALDI 17 Feb 1949; Maria, ROMA 22 Nov 1964, also known as MAFRICI. A7109: VITA POLISTENA, born 1919, per SURRIENTO, certificate 159164. J25 1971/4767: Polistena, Teresa, Brisbane. SP244/2: Vincenzo and Domenico Polistena, Sydney 1950, both with PHOTOGRAPHS ATTACHED. AND ONE ODDITY WORTH A LINE: B741 V/4249, «Misuse of letters of recall - Italian immigration», Melbourne 1927, whose description includes a newspaper article -- «DEATH DUEL WITH HOOKS - Guiseppe Antonio Cricri and Vincenzo Polistena». Not this family on any evidence, and recorded because a searcher meeting it later should not have to wonder.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete MELLUSO set, seventeen items
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on MELLUSO, written out in full. Queensland's own index returns exactly ONE Melluso registration, so this archive had Gregorio Melluso with no siblings and no children recorded anywhere in Australia.
result: SEVENTEEN ITEMS, AND TWO OF THEM NAME A HUSBAND THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HAVE. J25 1962/5930, Brisbane, 1952-1966: «PROSTAMO, DOMENICO FRANCESCO; WIFE ASSUNTE MARIA [NEE MELLUSO]». That is MARIA ASSUNTA MELLUSO, born about 1936 to Gregorio Melluso and Carmela Maria Borello, buried at Mount Gravatt in 1991 -- «the first Prostamo ever found in the Queensland index, and she was born a Melluso». HER HUSBAND'S NAME IS DOMENICO FRANCESCO PROSTAMO, and this is the first record of him. J25 1972/23086, Brisbane, 1959-1974: «MELLUSO, GREGORIO; WIFE CARMELA; AND CHILDREN GIUSEPPE, MARIA [SURNAME PROSTAMO]». Gregorio's own household, which Queensland's index could not show. «Wife Carmela» is Carmela Maria Borello. THE BRACKET IS AMBIGUOUS AND MUST NOT BE READ PAST: a daughter Maria carrying the surname Prostamo is simply Maria Assunta married; a SON Giuseppe carrying it is not, and would mean Carmela brought Prostamo children into the marriage. THE FILE TITLE IS A FINDING AID. Opening it would settle which, and it is «not yet examined». THE REST, WRITTEN OUT. SP1122/1 N1957/47306: Melluso, Rocco -- Italian migrant naturalisation file, Sydney, 1957-1963, «open with exception». MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWI49751: PRISONER OF WAR/INTERNEE MELLUSO, CARMELO, born 19 APRIL 1919, Italian, Melbourne -- a prisoner of war shipped to Australia, not a resident interned, and no evidence connects him here. BP289/1 001102370: Melluso, Giuseppe, arrived 29 February 1968 at Fremantle aboard GALILEO, file held at BRISBANE. A12038 995: PETRONIO-MELLUSO Felicia, born 25 September 1925. J25 1970/5204: PALMIERI, Antonio [born 1927]; wife VINCENZA [NEE MELLUSO] [born 1943]. C321 N1973/050286: Melluso, Carmela, Sydney. A9111 1981/1284: MELLUSO, Leonardo. B44 V1986/23418: Melluso, V, Melbourne. AND FIVE MELLUSO WOMEN ARE CATALOGUED UNDER MARRIED NAMES: Lucia DI BIASI «also known as Melluso»; Nicolina PAONE «also known as Melluso»; Domenica MELLUSO «also known as Patamia»; Vincenza MILETO «also known as Melluso»; and ORIANA (nee MELLUSO) Vicenta. THE SAME LESSON THE 1908 Scilla death index taught about Serafina Arlotta, in a different archive on the other side of the world: A MARRIED WOMAN IS INDEXED UNDER WHICHEVER NAME THE CLERK HAD, and a sweep that only reads the maiden surname column will miss her. Here the catalogue happens to carry both.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1828 atto 28 and the annual Tavola, read in full
scope: Giovanni Arlotta x Maria Costa's marriage — the act that would settle an eleven-year conflict in his age and decide whether the Domenico Arlotta generation belongs to this family. Found from the annual Tavola after 1829 was cleared and 1830 was not needed.
result: ACT 28 OF 1828, AND IT SETTLES MORE THAN IT WAS ASKED TO. Scilla, 30 AUGUST 1828: GIOVANNI ARLOTTA, DI ANNI VENTOTTO, marinaro, FIGLIO DI FU DOMENICO ARLOTTA E DI ANNA BARBARO; and MARIA COSTA, D'ANNI VENTISEI, FIGLIA DI ROCCO DI COSTA, marinaro, E DI PASQUALINA IDONE. Banns posted Sunday 3 August; church wedding 7 SEPTEMBER 1828 before D. Domenico Zanghi and Bruno Ingrigneri. THE BRIDE'S PARENTS ATTENDED AND CONSENTED IN PERSON -- so Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone were both alive and in the room. DOMENICO ARLOTTA IS CONFIRMED AND DATED. He is «FU Domenico» here, so DEAD BEFORE 30 AUGUST 1828, twenty-six years tighter than the «before April 1854» this archive carried -- and the generation is not dislodged, which was the real risk. THREE NEW PEOPLE: ANNA BARBARO, Giovanni's mother; ROCCO COSTA and PASQUALINA IDONE, Maria's parents. All three alive in 1828, none in the family tree. AND IT BREAKS TWO AGES, ONE OF THEM WRITTEN BY ME THIS MORNING. Giovanni Arlotta is TWENTY-EIGHT here (b. c. 1800), FORTY on his daughter's birth act of 1830, and SEVENTY-FIVE on his grandson's of 1854 -- three of his own declarations spanning twenty-one years. The marriage act is preferred. Twenty-eight in 1828 is thirty in 1830, and «trenta» written or read as «quaranta» is ordinary; the 1854 «settantacinque» is not, and stays open as either a badly wrong age or a second Giovanni Arlotta son of a late Domenico. MARIA COSTA is TWENTY-SIX here (b. c. 1802) and this archive entered her as «c. 1807» a few hours earlier off the 1830 act. CORRECTED, WITH THE OLD FIGURE LEFT ON THE RECORD. A CANDIDATE WITHDRAWN BY THE SAME ACT. A DOMENICO COSTA, commerciante, forty-six, witnessed Serafina's registration in 1830 and was recorded here as a candidate for Maria Costa's father, graded «candidate» precisely so it could be withdrawn. HER FATHER WAS ROCCO. That is what the grade was for. AND THE TAVOLA CLOSED ANOTHER ROW FOR FREE. The 1828 annual index names BOTH SPOUSES' PARENTS, and its FIRST entry is «ARENA ANTONIO e DE LUCA SERAFINA -- ORAZIO e MORABITO LETTERIA / FILIPPO e ALFONZETTI ANNA -- 10 Ag.o 1828 -- atto 26». That is the OTHER Antonio Arena married to a Serafina, the collision guarded this morning; his parents are ORAZIO ARENA and LETTERIA MORABITO, which is where that family's Orazio comes from. 1829's Tavola opens at B with no A section at all, so neither surname married that year.

source: Antenati — Scilla, Matrimoni 1851 Tavola annuale, entry 1, against the 1828 convention
scope: A direct test of a correction graded «inferred» that morning: were Filippo Arena, Domenica Costa, Giovanni Arlotta and Maria Costa alive when their children married in February 1851? The processetti bundle held no death act for any of them, which is an argument from absence.
result: CONFIRMED, AND BY A POSITIVE READING. Container LD6brxB, 96 images; the 1851 Tavola runs images 88-96 and ENTRY 1 IS «ARENA FRANCESCO e ARLOTTA SERAFINA», Scilla. Its parents column reads «FILIPPO, e COSTA DOMENICA» and «GIOVANNI e COSTA MARIA» -- both exactly right, and NEITHER CARRIES «FU». WHY THAT IS EVIDENCE AND NOT SILENCE. The same series marks the dead: the 1828 Tavola writes Giovanni Arlotta as son of «FU Dom.co e Barbaro Anna» -- father dead, mother living -- and «fu» appears on THIS PAGE of 1851 in other entries, including entry 4. The convention is in use locally and it is not applied to our four. THEY WERE ALL FOUR ALIVE IN FEBRUARY 1851. The morning's correction moves from «inferred» to «documented». AND THE INSTRUMENT IS BETTER THAN THIS ARCHIVE HAS BEEN TREATING IT. A Scilla marriage Tavola carries Num. d'ordine | Sposi | Patria | PROFESSIONE | GENITORI | Giorno della Celebrazione. One index opening therefore gives four parents AND dates the life status of all four, without opening an act. Every year of the restaurazione series will do this. ONE CAUTION FOR WHOEVER USES IT. The date column is the CHURCH celebration, not the civil act -- in 1828 the Tavola says 7 September where the civil promise was 30 August. An act number and a Tavola date will disagree by days or weeks and neither is wrong. AND THE ROWS ARE NOT CLEANLY ALIGNED: in 1851 the parents are written slightly above their own line and interleave with the neighbouring entry, so a parent pair must be matched to a spouse BY NAME, not by height on the page. Entry 1's four lines were disentangled that way.

source: Antenati — Scilla marriage indexes 1810, 1811, 1812, 1818, 1819 swept for Filippo Arena
scope: FILIPPO ARENA x DOMENICA COSTA'S MARRIAGE, which is the only route left to GENERATION NINE on the Scilla side. He was twenty-five and she twenty-seven when their son Francesco was born on 25 November 1819, so they married about 1812-1819. Four volumes' indexes checked; two more have none.
result: TWO CLEAN NEGATIVES AND A COVERAGE MAP. 1819 (container 0AJEJ8b, 79 images, Tavola at 75-79): alphabetised by SURNAME. Its A section holds ONE entry -- «Abbate Grazia e Capitano Giovanna», 8 Febraro. NO ARENA. 1818 (container LPaGar8, 43 images, Tavola at 41-43): alphabetised by the GROOM'S GIVEN NAME, exactly as this archive's cautions warn. FILIPPO THEREFORE SITS UNDER F, NOT A, and the F section is entries 10-13: Francesco Migliarino x Antonia Fulco (21 Gennaro), Francesco Polimeni x Clementina Perina (26 Gennaro), FILIPPO PIZZARELLO x Francesca Fava (27 Gennaro), Francesco La Valle x Nicola Florio (10 Aprile). NO FILIPPO ARENA. Searching the A section of 1818 would have produced a confident, complete and entirely false negative. 1817 (container 5K9P9J9, 43 images) HAS NO TAVOLA AT ALL -- the volume runs to act 41 and then blank forms. 1816 (container wQYJYDb, 45 images) LIKEWISE: acts to 42, then blanks, and the archivist's card reads VOLUME TARLATO, worm-eaten. SO THE UNREAD GROUND IS: 1816 and 1817, which cost a full act-by-act read of about forty openings apiece because there is no index to shortcut; and the NAPOLEONIC years 1809-1815, whose containers have not been bought (arks in scilla-arks.tsv). Scilla's registers begin in 1809, not 1816, so those years exist. ALL FOUR CONTAINERS ARE NOW SAVED so no later session pays for them again. EXTENDED THE SAME DAY INTO THE NAPOLEONIC FONDO, AND THREE MORE YEARS FALL. 1812 (container wX9PERp, 23 images, Tavola at 22-23): SEVENTEEN marriages, alphabetised by the GROOM'S GIVEN NAME. All seventeen read. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1811 (container wl1gvZD, 19 images, Tavola at 18-19): same ordering. Its F section is Ferdinando di Franco, Francesco Arbitrio and Fulcantonio Bova. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1810 (container LzjyVKj, 18 images, INDICE at 17-18): same ordering. Its F section is Filippo LAGANA, Francesco Vita, Francesco Martello, Francesco Zirilli and a Francesco Fa[va]. THERE IS A FILIPPO AND HE IS A LAGANA. NO FILIPPO ARENA. 1809 (container LD6vJel, 29 images) HAS NO TAVOLA -- acts to 27, then blank forms. SO THE MARRIAGE IS NOT IN 1810, 1811, 1812, 1818 OR 1819, and the unindexed years left are 1809, 1813-1814, 1815, 1816 and 1817. ALL NINE CONTAINERS ARE NOW SAVED. AND THE SWEEP PAID FOR ITSELF SIDEWAYS. The 1811 Tavola gives «GIOVANNI VILARDI x CANDIDA COSTA -- Gaetano ed Antonia Mellica / ROCCO e PASQUALINA IDONE». Rocco Costa and Pasqualina Idone are MARIA COSTA'S PARENTS, read three hours earlier off the 1828 marriage act. SO CANDIDA COSTA IS MARIA COSTA'S SISTER, married at Scilla in 1811 -- a generation-seven sibling found for free, in an index opened for somebody else. FOUR MORE SCILLA HOUSEHOLDS NOTED IN PASSING, none of them joined to this family: CARLO ARENA x EUGENIA GRAJA, whose daughter Giovanna married Giovanni La Mussa in January 1812; a «fu ANTONIA ARENA» named as a mother in 1812; NATALINA ARENA, a mother in 1811; and ANNA ARLOTTA, a mother in 1811. Carlo Arena is of roughly the right generation to be Filippo Arena's father and there is NOTHING WHATEVER to support that beyond the surname and the town -- recorded so the next session does not rediscover him and think it has found something.

source: NAA NameSearch — the complete MAZZA set, two hundred items, written out
scope: NameSearch, all record categories, on MAZZA, read out at 200 to a page. Swept once before and summarised; this pass exists to write the family-plausible items down.
result: TWO HUNDRED ITEMS. Four are prisoner-of-war files for men born in Italy and captured in Africa, unconnected. Of the rest, these are the ones that touch this family. ANDREA MAZZA IS DATED AT LAST. NAA: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA A: «Mazza, Andrea - Nationality: Italian - NATURALISATION CERTIFICATE GRANTED 27 NOVEMBER 1934», held at Brisbane. Row 106 has him only as a TIMBER CUTTER AT CARDWELL on the 1959 electoral roll, a lead a roll could not settle. He was naturalised in Queensland TWENTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER, and naturalisation of that period wanted about five years' residence, so he was in Australia by about 1929. He is not a post-war arrival and not a stranger passing through. IT STILL DOES NOT MAKE HIM A RELATIVE -- the certificate names no parents -- but it turns a single roll line into a man with two dates. AND MARIO MAZZA WITH HIM: BP4/3, ITALIAN MAZZA M, naturalisation certificate granted 11 NOVEMBER 1927. That fits the Mario Mazza who married Peppina Mazzaglia in Queensland in 1924 and whose son Rosario was born there in 1925. WHAT HAPPENED TO ROSARIO MAZZA AFTER THE CAMP. NAA: J1737, MAZZA R: «Mazza Rosario, CAS 15000 - CIVIL ALIENS CORPS (CAC)», Brisbane, 1944, ACCESS OPEN. The Civil Aliens Corps is the labour corps internees were released into, and this archive had his internment dossier (MP1103/1, Q8110) and nothing after it. A service number, CAS 15000, and a file. OTHER FAMILY-PLAUSIBLE ITEMS. A261 1948/625: «Applicant - MAZZA Rosario; Nominee - PAGLIARO Carmela; PAGLIARO Loretta Donna Maria» -- Rosario sponsoring two women into Australia in 1948. J25 1962/1887: «Mazza, Giuseppe, Sebastiano, Stefano and Graziella», Brisbane. J25 1970/5500: «Applicant: Mazza, SEBASTIANO; Nominee: Napoli, Mario and wife Maria [NEE COCO]» -- and a Maria Mazza married a Rosario COCO in Queensland in 1939, so the Coco are in this circle twice. J25 1966/11584: «Mazza, Angelo; wife Francesca [nee Strano]; and child Giovanni» -- Angelo Mazza and Francesca Strano are already in the Queensland death index as Giovanni Mazza's parents. J25 1951/10120 and B78 ITALIAN/MAZZA SERAFINO GIOVANNI: Serafino Giovanni Mazza, arrived BRISBANE per SYDNEY 3 April 1952. BP145/1: Antonio Mazza, born 25 January 1935, arrived CAIRNS on the AURELIA, May 1956. BP25/1 ITALIAN SPATARO G: «Spataro [nee Mazza], Grazia», arrived Sydney on the Sebastiano Caboto 9 February 1951. A FINDING AID WORTH KNOWING: NAA BP628/5, «Name Index and registration cards for internees dossiers QUEENSLAND - MACAUDO to MYSLIM», 1939-1962, Brisbane, OPEN. That is the index to the Queensland internee dossiers, and MAZZA falls inside its range. TWO GUARDS. A12508 31/3204 is a DIFFERENT ROSARIO MAZZA, born 1 FEBRUARY 1877, arriving Melbourne per VIMINALE on 10 July 1939 -- twenty-two years older than this archive's Rosario and landing at the wrong port in the same decade. A12508 31/3203 is an IRIS MAZZA, born 4 December 1915, arriving Brisbane per ROMOLO on 26 December 1939. Neither is anybody here.

source: NAA — the Crupi internment dossiers, and a Civil Aliens Corps hypothesis tested and failed
scope: A direct test of a hypothesis published an hour earlier: that the Crupi brothers, released from internment in late 1943, would have Civil Aliens Corps files in NAA series J1737 as Rosario Mazza does.
result: THE HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG. The complete CRUPI name index — 233 items, all read — contains NO J1737 ITEM, NO «Civil Aliens Corps» and NO CAS service number for any Crupi. Rosario Mazza has one; neither of his wife's brothers does. Recorded as a negative rather than quietly dropped, because it was published as a plan and somebody would otherwise look for it again. WHAT IT MIGHT MEAN is unresolved: the Corps was not universal, and men released in October and December 1943 may simply have gone home to the cane. BUT THE SEARCH ANSWERED A BETTER QUESTION. ANTONINO CRUPI'S INTERNMENT DOSSIER IS NAA: MP1103/1, Q7838 — «Prisoner of War/Internee: Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 05 November 1907», Melbourne, 1942-1943, ACCESS OPEN; with its companion MP1103/2, Q7838. AND THE NUMBER CLOSES THE LOOP: his ALIENS REGISTRATION CARD, read this morning, carries «Q. 7838» beside his name. Same man, two series, one number. The identification no longer rests on birthplace alone. MARIO CRUPI LIKEWISE: MP1103/2, Q30124 — «Crupi, Mario; Year of birth - 1905». His aliens card gives «N.B.E. certificate Q30124». Same closure. A CONFLICT TO FLAG, NOT TO RESOLVE. The card gives Antonino's date of birth as «5.10.07» — 5 OCTOBER 1907 in Australian order. The dossier catalogue says «05 NOVEMBER 1907». One month apart, both from Commonwealth paperwork about the same man. The dossier itself would settle it; neither figure is preferred here. AND A THIRD ANTONIO CRUPI, WHO IS NOT OURS. MP1103/1 and MP1103/2, PWV11028: «Crupi, Antonio; Date of birth - 10 January 1904», a VICTORIAN internee — the PWV prefix against our Q. That is now the THIRD man of that name this archive has had to set aside, after the Serrata card at barcode 9209609 and the Silkwood East farmer on the 1959 roll. FINDING AID: NAA BP628/5, «Name Index and registration cards for internees dossiers Queensland - CACCIOLA to CURSIO», 1939-1962, Brisbane, OPEN. CRUPI falls inside that range, as MAZZA falls inside MACAUDO-MYSLIM.
